title.zh: 卷500 列傳二百八十七 遗逸一
title.raw: 卷500 列傳二百八十七 遗逸一

sentences.zh: 李清李模梁以樟王世德閻爾梅萬壽祺鄭與僑

translations.literal: Li Qing, Li Mo, Liang Yizhang, Wang Shide, Yan Ermei, Wan Shouqi, Zheng Yiqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qing, Li Mo, Liang Yizhang, Wang Shide, Yan Ermei, Wan Shouqi, and Zheng Yiqiao.

sentences.zh: 曹元方莊元辰王玉藻李長祥王正中董守諭

translations.literal: Cao Yuanfang, Zhuang Yuanchen, Wang Yuzao, Li Changxiang, Wang Zhengzhong, Dong Shouyu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuanfang, Zhuang Yuanchen, Wang Yuzao, Li Changxiang, Wang Zhengzhong, and Dong Shouyu.

sentences.zh: 陸宇弟宇巇江漢方以智子中德等錢澄之

translations.literal: Lu Yu, his younger brother Lu Xi, Jiang Han, Fang Yizhi and his son Zhongde and others, Qian Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu, his younger brother Lu Xi, Jiang Han, Fang Yizhi and his son Zhongde among others, and Qian Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 惲日初郭金台硃之瑜沈光文陳士京吳祖錫

translations.literal: Yun Richu, Guo Jintai, Zhu Zhiyu, Shen Guangwen, Chen Shijing, Wu Zuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Richu, Guo Jintai, Zhu Zhiyu, Shen Guangwen, Chen Shijing, and Wu Zuxi.

sentences.zh: 太史公伯夷列傳，憂憤悲嘆，百世下猶想見其人。

translations.literal: In the Grand Historian's biography of Bo Yi, grief, indignation, sorrow, and lamentation are such that even a hundred generations later one still longs to behold the man.
translations.idiomatic: In the Grand Historian's account of Bo Yi, the grief and righteous anger are so vivid that even centuries later readers still feel as though they could meet the man face to face.

sentences.zh: 伯夷、叔齊扣馬而諫，既不能行其志，不得已乃遁西山，歌采薇，痛心疾首，豈果自甘餓死哉？

translations.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi seized the horse's bridle to remonstrate; unable to carry out their purpose, they had no choice but to flee to Mount Xi, singing of gathering fern shoots, heartsick to the marrow—did they truly resign themselves to starving to death?
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi and Shu Qi seized the reins to remonstrate with the new ruler; when they could not prevail, they withdrew to Mount Xi and sang of gathering wild greens, heartsick with anguish. Did they truly choose starvation of their own free will?

sentences.zh: 清初，代明平賊，順天應人，得天下之正，古未有也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing, replacing the Ming and pacifying the rebels, conforming to Heaven and responding to the people, they obtained the orthodox possession of the realm—never before seen in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Qing, the new dynasty replaced the Ming, pacified the rebels, aligned itself with Heaven and won the people's assent, and secured legitimate rule over the empire—an achievement without precedent in history.

sentences.zh: 天命既定，遺臣逸士猶不惜九死一生以圖再造，及事​​不成，雖浮海入山，而回天之志終不少衰。

translations.literal: Once the Mandate of Heaven was settled, surviving ministers and reclusive scholars still did not spare nine deaths for one life in plotting restoration; when affairs failed, though they took to the sea or entered the mountains, their will to turn back Heaven never diminished in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the Mandate had clearly shifted, loyalist officials and reclusive scholars risked death again and again to restore the fallen dynasty; when restoration failed, they fled across the sea or into the mountains, yet their resolve to reverse Heaven's decree never waned.

sentences.zh: 迄於國亡已數十年，呼號奔走，逐墜日以終其身，至老死不變，何其壯歟！

translations.literal: Down to several decades after the state's fall, crying out and rushing about, they pursued their cause day by day until the end of their lives, unchanging even unto old age and death—how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Decades after the dynasty had fallen, they still cried out and strove on, pursuing their cause to the end of their days without ever wavering even in old age—how magnificent their spirit was!

sentences.zh: 今為遺逸傳，凡明末遺臣如李清等，逸士如李孔昭等，分著於篇，雖寥寥數十人，皆大節凜然，足風後世者也。

translations.literal: Now composing biographies of recluses, in all late-Ming surviving ministers such as Li Qing and reclusive scholars such as Li Kongzhao, each set forth in separate sections—though only a few dozen in number, all possessed stern integrity sufficient to instruct later generations.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter records the recluses: late-Ming loyalist officials such as Li Qing and withdrawn scholars such as Li Kongzhao, each treated in turn. Though only a few dozen in all, every one upheld unyielding integrity worthy to inspire posterity.

sentences.zh: 至黃宗羲等已見儒林傳，魏禧等已見文苑傳，餘或分見於孝友及藝術諸傳，則當比而觀之，以見其全焉。

translations.literal: As for Huang Zongxi and others, they already appear in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars; Wei Xi and others already appear in the Biographies of Literary Men; the rest appear separately in the filial and artistic biographies—one should compare these accounts to see them whole.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongxi and others already have entries among the Confucian scholars; Wei Xi and others among the men of letters; still others appear in the chapters on filial devotion and the arts. Readers should consult those biographies together with this one to grasp each man's full character.

sentences.zh: 李清，字心水，號映碧，興化人。

translations.literal: Li Qing, courtesy name Xinshui, style name Yingbi, was a native of Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qing, whose courtesy name was Xinshui and style name Yingbi, came from Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 天啟辛酉舉人，崇禎辛未進士，授寧波府推官。

translations.literal: In the xinyou year of the Tianqi reign he passed the provincial examination; in the xinwei year of the Chongzhen reign he became a jinshi and was appointed investigating censor of Ningbo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the xinyou year of Tianqi and became a jinshi in the xinwei year of Chongzhen, after which he was appointed investigating censor of Ningbo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 考最，擢刑科給事中，同日上兩疏：一言禦外敵當戰守兼治，不當輕言款；

translations.literal: Rated highest in evaluation, he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments; on the same day he submitted two memorials: one saying that in resisting external enemies warfare and defense should be pursued together, and one should not lightly speak of negotiated peace;
translations.idiomatic: Rated top in his performance review, he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments. That same day he submitted two memorials. In the first he argued that resisting foreign enemies required combining offensive and defensive measures, and that the court must not speak lightly of negotiated peace;

sentences.zh: 禦內寇當剿撫並用，不當專言撫。

translations.literal: in resisting internal bandits suppression and appeasement should be used together, and one should not speak only of appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: in the second he argued that suppressing internal rebels required both military action and conciliation, and that the court must not rely on appeasement alone.

sentences.zh: 一言治獄不宜置失入，而獨罪失出，因論尚書劉之鳳不職狀。

translations.literal: one saying that in administering justice one should not overlook wrongful convictions while punishing only wrongful acquittals, and thereby discussed the dereliction of Minister Liu Zhifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the courts should not ignore wrongful convictions while punishing only wrongful acquittals, and used the occasion to denounce the dereliction of Minister Liu Zhifeng.

sentences.zh: 尋以天旱，复疏言此用刑鍛鍊刻深所致，語侵尚書甄淑，淑遂劾清把持，詔鐫級，調浙江布政司照磨。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of drought, he again memorialized that this was caused by severe torture and harsh punishment in criminal cases, his words impugning Minister Zhen Shu; Shu then impeached Qing for domineering conduct, and an edict reduced his rank and transferred him to be assistant registrar in the Zhejiang provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: When drought followed, he memorialized again that the disaster stemmed from excessive torture and harsh sentencing, implicating Minister Zhen Shu. Shu retaliated by impeaching Qing for abusing his office, and the throne reduced his rank and transferred him to an assistant registrar post in the Zhejiang provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 無何，淑敗，即家起吏科給事中。

translations.literal: Before long Shu fell, and Qing was summoned from home to be supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shu fell from power, and Qing was recalled from retirement to serve as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 疾朝臣日競門戶，疏言：「國家門戶有二：北門之鎖鑰，以三協為門戶；

translations.literal: Distressed that court officials daily contended in factional strife, he memorialized: "The state has two gateways: the lock and key of the northern gate, with the three frontier garrisons as the gateway;
translations.idiomatic: Distressed by the daily factional strife among court officials, he memorialized: "The realm has two gates that must be defended. The northern gate is secured by the three frontier garrisons;

sentences.zh: 陪京之扃鍵，以兩淮為門戶。

translations.literal: the bolt and bar of the auxiliary capital, with the two Huai regions as the gateway.
translations.idiomatic: the secondary capital is secured by the two Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 置此不問，而閧堂斫穴，長此安底？

translations.literal: Leaving these unattended while brawling in the hall and hacking at one another's burrows—how can this go on?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you ignore these vital defenses while officials brawl in court and tear at one another's factions. How can this continue?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，不報。

translations.literal: " The memorial entered; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，福王建號南京，遷工科都給事中。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, the Prince of Fu established his reign at Nanjing; Qing was transferred to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Beijing fell, the Prince of Fu proclaimed his regime at Nanjing, and Qing was promoted to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 見朝政日壞，官方大亂，乃疏言：「大仇未雪，凡乘國難以拜官者，義將慚慟入地，宜急更前轍，以圖光復。

translations.literal: Seeing court affairs daily worsen and officialdom in great disorder, he memorialized: "The great enmity has not been avenged; all who seized office amid national calamity should, in righteousness, be ashamed unto death in the earth; you should urgently change your former course to plan restoration."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the court deteriorate daily and officialdom fall into chaos, he memorialized: "Our great enemy remains unavenged. Every man who accepted office amid national catastrophe ought to die of shame. Your Majesty must urgently change course and strive for restoration."

sentences.zh: 」又憤時議以偏安自足，抗疏曰：「昔宋高之南渡也，說者謂其病於意足，若陛下於今日，其何足之有？

translations.literal: " Again, indignant that current opinion took partial security as sufficient, he submitted a forceful memorial: "When Emperor Gaozong of Song crossed south, critics said his fault lay in being content in mind; if Your Majesty today, what contentment is there?
translations.idiomatic: " Indignant that contemporaries were content with mere territorial survival, he submitted a forceful memorial: "When Emperor Gaozong fled south, critics said his fatal flaw was complacency. What grounds for complacency does Your Majesty have today?

sentences.zh: 以河、洛為豐、沛，則恭皇之舊封也，為恭皇所已有而不有，則不足；

translations.literal: Taking the He and Luo as Feng and Pei, these were the former fiefs of the Respectful Emperor—what the Respectful Emperor already possessed yet does not possess, then there is not sufficiency;
translations.idiomatic: If you regard the He and Luo regions as your Feng and Pei, they were the former domains of the Respectful Emperor—territory he once held but you do not. How can that be called enough?

sentences.zh: 以金陵為長安，則高帝之始基也，為高帝所全有而不有，則不足。

translations.literal: taking Jinling as Chang'an, this was the founding base of the High Emperor—what the High Emperor fully possessed yet does not possess, then there is not sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: If you regard Jinling as Chang'an, it was the founding capital of the dynastic founder—territory he once held in full but you do not. That too falls far short of enough.

sentences.zh: 臣深望陛下無忘痛恥，以此志為中外倡也。

translations.literal: Your servant deeply hopes Your Majesty will not forget pain and shame, and take this resolve as a model for court and realm.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly beg Your Majesty never to forget this humiliation, and to make that resolve the standard for the entire court and realm.

sentences.zh: 儻陛下弛於上，則諸臣必逸於下，先帝之深仇，將安得而復哉？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty relaxes above, then the ministers will surely grow lax below—how will the late emperor's deep enmity ever be avenged?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty slackens above, your ministers will grow lax below. How then will the late emperor's deep wrong ever be avenged?

sentences.zh: 且宋之南渡，猶走李成，擒楊麼，以靖內製外。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Song crossed south, they still routed Li Cheng and captured Yang Mo, pacifying the interior to control the exterior.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the Song fled south, they still routed Li Cheng and captured Yang Mo, pacifying internal threats before confronting external enemies.

sentences.zh: 今則獻、瑤交熾，兩川危於累卵，汀、潮、南贛，並以警聞。

translations.literal: Now Xian and Yao blaze together, the two Sichuans are perilous as piled eggs, and Ting, Chao, and southern Gan all report alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Today Zhang Xianzhong and Jin Shenghong rage unchecked, the two Sichuans hang by a thread, and alarms pour in from Tingzhou, Chaozhou, and southern Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 北有既毀之室，南無可怡之堂，臣竊為陛下危之！

translations.literal: In the north there is a house already destroyed; in the south there is no hall in which to take ease—your servant privately fears for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: The north is a ruin, and the south offers no secure refuge. I tremble for Your Majesty's peril!

sentences.zh: 」疏上，報聞而已。

translations.literal: " The memorial went up; acknowledgment of receipt was all.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted, but the court merely noted its receipt and took no action.

sentences.zh: 有司始諡莊烈帝為思宗，清言廟號同於漢後主禪，請易之。

translations.literal: The authorities first gave the posthumous title Sizong to the Zhuanglie Emperor; Qing said the temple name was the same as that of the Han Later Lord Liu Shan and requested it be changed.
translations.idiomatic: When officials first gave the late emperor the temple name Sizong, Qing objected that it echoed the name of the Han's last ruler Liu Shan and petitioned for a change.

sentences.zh: 又請補諡太子、二王及開國、靖難並累朝死諫諸臣，或以為迂，歎曰：「士大夫廉恥喪盡矣！

translations.literal: He also requested supplementary posthumous titles for the crown prince, the two princes, and ministers who died remonstrating from the founding, the Jingnan campaign, and successive reigns; some thought this pedantic, and he sighed: "The integrity and shame of scholar-officials are utterly lost!
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned for posthumous honors for the crown prince, the two princes, and loyal ministers who died remonstrating from the founding reign through the Jingnan crisis and later dynasties. Some dismissed this as pedantic. He sighed: "Scholar-officials have lost every shred of integrity and shame!

sentences.zh: 不於此時顯微闡幽，激發忠義之氣，更復何望耶？

translations.literal: If not at this time to bring the obscure to light and rouse the spirit of loyalty and righteousness, what further hope is there?
translations.idiomatic: If we do not now bring hidden loyalty to light and stir the spirit of righteous devotion, what hope remains?

sentences.zh: 」清事兩朝，凡三居諫職，章奏後先數十上，並寢閣不行。

translations.literal: " Qing served two reigns, thrice holding remonstrance office; memorials and reports numbering several tens in succession were all shelved in the privy council and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: " Qing served two reigns and held remonstrance office three times. He submitted dozens of memorials in succession, but every one was shelved in the privy council and never acted upon.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大理寺左寺丞，遣祀南鎮，行甫及杭，而南都失守矣。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to left assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and dispatched to sacrifice at the Southern Sacred Mountain; he had just reached Hangzhou when the southern capital was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to left assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and sent to perform sacrifices at the Southern Sacred Mountain. He had only reached Hangzhou when the southern capital fell.

sentences.zh: 乃由間道趨隱松江，又渡江寓高郵，久乃歸故園，杜門不與人事。

translations.literal: He then took bypaths to seek seclusion in Songjiang, crossed the river to lodge at Gaoyou, and after a long while returned to his native place, shutting his door and having no dealings with worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He fled by back roads to hide in Songjiang, then crossed the Yangzi to stay at Gaoyou. Only after a long interval did he return home, where he shut his door and withdrew from public life entirely.

sentences.zh: 當道屢薦不起，凡​​三十有八年而歿。

translations.literal: Local authorities repeatedly recommended him, but he would not rise; in all thirty-eight years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Local authorities repeatedly recommended him for office, but he always refused. Thirty-eight years later he died.

sentences.zh: 清忠義蓋出天性，莊烈帝之變，適在揚州，聞之，號慟幾絕。

translations.literal: Qing's loyalty and righteousness sprang from his inborn nature; the Zhuanglie Emperor's calamity happened to occur while he was in Yangzhou—on hearing it, he wailed until nearly breathless.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's loyalty sprang from his very nature. When the Zhuanglie Emperor met his calamity, Qing happened to be in Yangzhou; on hearing the news he wailed until he nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 自是每遇三月十九日，必設位以哭。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever the nineteenth day of the third month came, he invariably set out a seat and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, on the nineteenth day of the third month each year, he always set out a memorial seat and wept.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾家世受國恩，吾以外吏，蒙先帝簡擢，涓埃未報。

translations.literal: He once said: "My family for generations received the state's grace; I, a minor official, was specially elevated by the late emperor, yet not even a drop of dust have I repaid.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "My family has received the state's grace for generations. Though only a minor official, I was personally elevated by the late emperor, yet I repaid that debt with less than a speck of dust.

sentences.zh: 」國亡後，守其硜硜，有死無二，蓋以此也。

translations.literal: " After the state's fall, he held to his unyielding integrity, loyal unto death without wavering—this was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " After the dynasty fell, he held to his unyielding integrity and would rather die than serve another regime. That was why.

sentences.zh: 晚著書自娛，尤潛心史學，為史論若干卷，又刪注南、北二史，編次南渡錄等書，藏於家。

translations.literal: In his later years he wrote books for his own pleasure, especially devoting himself to historical studies; he composed several scrolls of historical essays, also abridged and annotated the two histories of the Northern and Southern Dynasties, compiled the Record of the Southern Crossing and other works, and kept them at home.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he wrote for his own solace, devoting himself especially to historical studies. He produced several scrolls of historical essays, abridged and annotated the Northern and Southern Dynasties histories, compiled works such as the Record of the Southern Crossing, and kept them in his private collection.

sentences.zh: 李模，字子木，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Li Mo, courtesy name Zimu, was a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mo, whose courtesy name was Zimu, came from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 天啟乙丑進士，授東莞知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the yichou year of Tianqi, he was appointed magistrate of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the yichou year of Tianqi and was appointed magistrate of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 考最，入為御史。

translations.literal: Rated highest in evaluation, he entered the capital as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Rated top in his performance review, he was summoned to the capital as a censor.

sentences.zh: 因劾論中官，謫南京國子監典籍。

translations.literal: Because he impeached and discussed eunuch officials, he was demoted to archivist of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After he impeached the eunuch faction, he was demoted to archivist of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 福王立，封四鎮為侯、伯，模上言：「擁立時，陛下不以得位為利，諸臣何敢以定策為功？

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was established, the four frontier garrisons were enfeoffed as marquises and earls; Mo memorialized: "At the time of enthronement, Your Majesty did not regard gaining the throne as profit—how dare the ministers claim merit for fixing the succession?
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu took the throne, the four frontier commanders were enfeoffed as marquises and earls. Mo memorialized: "When Your Majesty was enthroned, you did not treat the throne as personal gain. How then can your ministers claim merit for having fixed the succession?

sentences.zh: 甚至侯、伯之封，輕加鎮將。

translations.literal: To go so far as marquis and earl enfeoffments, lightly bestowed on garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: To enfeoff frontier commanders as marquises and earls so lightly is indefensible.

sentences.zh: 夫諸將事先帝未收桑榆之效，事陛下未彰汗馬之績，方應戴罪，何有勳勞？

translations.literal: These generals served the late emperor without achieving the effect of the evening mulberry; they serve Your Majesty without displaying sweat-of-the-horse achievements—they ought rather to bear guilt; what merit have they?
translations.idiomatic: These generals achieved nothing for the late emperor in his final years and have won no distinction under Your Majesty. They ought to stand accused, not rewarded. What merit have they?

sentences.zh: 使諸將果忠義者，必先慰先帝殉國之靈，而後可膺陛下延世之賞。

translations.literal: If the generals were truly loyal and righteous, they must first comfort the spirit of the late emperor who died for the state, and only then may they receive Your Majesty's rewards for prolonging the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: If they were truly loyal, they would first comfort the spirit of the emperor who died for the realm, and only then accept Your Majesty's rewards for preserving the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」報聞。

translations.literal: " Acknowledgment of receipt was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The court merely noted receipt of the memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋改為河南道御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to censor of the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to censor of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 馬、阮亂政，歎曰：「事無可為矣！

translations.literal: When Ma and Ruan threw the government into disorder, he sighed: "Affairs can no longer be accomplished!
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Shiying and Ruan Dayue threw the government into chaos, he sighed: "There is nothing left to be done!

sentences.zh: 」即請告，不復出。

translations.literal: " He immediately requested leave and never came forth again.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately requested leave and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 杜門里居，三十年如一日。

translations.literal: He shut his door and lived at home, thirty years like a single day.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his door and lived in seclusion at home for thirty years without wavering.

sentences.zh: 幼與徐汧為總角交，汧死國事，為卹其家而存其孤，不渝舊好。

translations.literal: In youth he was a childhood friend of Xu Kan; when Kan died for the state, Mo provided for his family and preserved his orphan, never changing their old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had been close friends with Xu Kan. When Kan died for the state, Mo supported his family and raised his orphaned son, never betraying their old bond.

sentences.zh: 年八十，卒於家。

translations.literal: At age eighty he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 梁以樟，字公狄，清苑人。

translations.literal: Liang Yizhang, courtesy name Gongdi, was a native of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yizhang, whose courtesy name was Gongdi, came from Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 與兄以棻、弟以桂，並知名，時號「三梁」。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Yifen and younger brother Yigui, all were renowned, and the age called them "the Three Liangs."
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Yifen and younger brother Yigui were all celebrated, and contemporaries called them "the Three Liangs."

sentences.zh: 以樟負異才，八歲讀書家塾中，值壁裂，作壁裂歌云：「壁猛裂，龍驚出。

translations.literal: Yizhang possessed extraordinary talent; at eight, studying in the family school, when a wall cracked he composed a Song of the Cracked Wall: "The wall fiercely splits—the dragon startles forth."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhang possessed extraordinary talent. At eight, while studying in the family school, he saw a wall crack and composed a Song of the Cracked Wall: "The wall splits apart—the startled dragon bursts forth."

sentences.zh: 」見者大奇之。

translations.literal: " Those who saw it greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: " All who heard it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 十六歲補弟子員，受知左光斗。

translations.literal: At sixteen he became a student member, gaining the recognition of Zuo Guangdou.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he became a licentiate and won the patronage of Zuo Guangdou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎己卯舉鄉試第一，明年成進士。

translations.literal: In the jimao year of Chongzhen he placed first in the provincial examination; the next year he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the jimao year of Chongzhen he ranked first in the provincial examination, and the following year became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 命試騎射，進士皆書生，夙不習，以樟獨躍馬彎弓，矢三發，的皆應弦破，觀者嘆異。

translations.literal: Ordered to test horsemanship and archery, the jinshi were all scholars long unpracticed; Yizhang alone leaped on a horse, bent the bow, and with three arrows loosed, each target broke at the bowstring—onlookers sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to demonstrate horsemanship and archery, the new jinshi—mere scholars untrained in arms—faltered. Yizhang alone vaulted into the saddle, drew his bow, and with three arrows shattered every target. The onlookers gasped in admiration.

sentences.zh: 即授河南太康知縣。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed magistrate of Taikang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed magistrate of Taikang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 中原盜起十餘年，所在荼毒，督撫莫能辦，率倡撫議，苟且幸無事，盜且服且叛。

translations.literal: Bandits had risen in the central plains for more than ten years; everywhere they ravaged; governors-general and governors could not cope, generally advocating appeasement, temporizing in hope of no trouble—the bandits both submitted and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry had scourged the central plains for more than a decade. Governors could not suppress it and generally favored appeasement, hoping merely to avoid immediate disaster while rebels submitted one day and revolted the next.

sentences.zh: 而河南比年大旱蝗，人相食，民益蜂起為盜。

translations.literal: Henan in recent years suffered great drought and locusts; men ate one another, and the people increasingly swarmed up as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Henan had suffered drought and locust plagues for years; men resorted to cannibalism, and the people rose in ever greater numbers as bandits.

sentences.zh: 人為以樟危，僉都御史史可法以其有經世略，獨勸之行。

translations.literal: People considered Yizhang in peril; the censor-in-chief Shi Kefa, because he had statecraft capacity, alone urged him to go.
translations.idiomatic: Many thought the appointment would doom Yizhang, but Censor-in-Chief Shi Kefa, recognizing his talent for statecraft, alone urged him to accept.

sentences.zh: 抵任，探知境內賊凡三十六窟，於是練鄉勇，修城堡，嚴保甲；

translations.literal: On reaching his post, he investigated and learned that within the district there were thirty-six bandit lairs in all; he then drilled local militia, repaired fortresses, and tightened the baojia system;
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he discovered thirty-six bandit strongholds within his jurisdiction. He drilled local militia, repaired fortifications, and tightened the baojia neighborhood defense system;

sentences.zh: 募死士，入賊巢。

translations.literal: recruited dare-to-die men, and sent them into bandit nests.
translations.idiomatic: recruited dare-to-die fighters and sent them into the bandit lairs.

sentences.zh: 伺賊出入。

translations.literal: They watched the bandits' comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: They spied on the rebels' movements.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜半馳風雪中，帥健兒密搗賊壘，賊驚佚，擒其渠，毀巢而歸。

translations.literal: Once at midnight he galloped through wind and snow, leading stalwart men to secretly strike a bandit camp; the bandits fled in alarm, he captured their chieftain, destroyed the nest, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Once at midnight he rode through wind and snow at the head of his best fighters, struck a bandit camp by surprise, captured its chieftain as the rest fled, destroyed the stronghold, and returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 居半載，境內賊悉平。

translations.literal: Within half a year, bandits throughout the district were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year he had pacified every bandit stronghold in the district.

sentences.zh: 調商丘，時李自成犯開封，不能破，乃東攻歸德。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shangqiu; at that time Li Zicheng attacked Kaifeng but could not take it, and therefore turned east to attack Guide.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shangqiu. Li Zicheng was then besieging Kaifeng without success and turned east to attack Guide.

sentences.zh: 以樟嬰城血戰三日夜，城陷，妻張率家人三十口自焚死，事具明史。

translations.literal: Yizhang defended the city in bloody battle for three days and nights; the city fell, and his wife Zhang led thirty members of the family to burn themselves to death—the affair is fully recorded in the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhang held the city in bloody combat for three days and nights. When it fell, his wife Zhang led thirty family members in self-immolation. The full account appears in the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 以樟被重創，僕亂屍中，死复甦，商民救之出，奔淮上，被逮讞請室。

translations.literal: Yizhang suffered grave wounds and fell among the corpses; dead, he revived; merchants rescued him and brought him out; he fled to the Huai region and was arrested and sent to the prison for capital cases.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhang was gravely wounded and lay among the dead until he revived. Local merchants rescued him and he fled to the Huai region, where he was arrested and thrown into prison on a capital charge.

sentences.zh: 賊入潼關，复渡河東犯，京師震動。

translations.literal: The bandits entered Tong Pass, again crossed the river and attacked eastward, and the capital was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels entered Tong Pass, crossed the Yellow River again, and advanced eastward, throwing the capital into panic.

sentences.zh: 以樟乃從獄中上疏：「請皇太子撫軍南京，輔以重臣，假便宜從事，係人心。

translations.literal: Yizhang then from prison submitted a memorial: "I request that the crown prince command troops at Nanjing, assisted by high ministers, granted discretionary authority—to bind the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: From prison Yizhang submitted a memorial: "I urge that the crown prince take command at Nanjing, assisted by senior ministers with discretionary authority, to steady the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 倡召豪傑義旅，大起勤王兵。

translations.literal: Advocate summoning heroic volunteers and righteous armies, and greatly raise troops to rescue the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Summon loyal volunteers and raise a great army to rescue the throne.

sentences.zh: 擇宗室賢才，分建要地，而重督撫權，行方鎮遺意，合力拒。

translations.literal: Select worthy talent among the imperial clan, establish them at key places, and strengthen the authority of governors-general and governors, following the intent of the Tang frontier commands, to resist together.
translations.idiomatic: Select worthy princes of the blood, station them at strategic points, and restore the broad authority of frontier commanders after the Tang model, so that all forces may resist together."

sentences.zh: 」疏上，執政尼之。

translations.literal: " The memorial went up; the chief ministers blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted, but the chief ministers blocked it.

sentences.zh: 迨出獄，而都城陷。

translations.literal: When he came out of prison, the capital had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he left prison, the capital had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 福王立，以樟自德州、臨清南下，與各郡邑建義文武吏及諸豪士歃血盟，人皆感憤流涕，受約束待命。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was established, Yizhang came south from Dezhou and Linqing, and with civil and military officials and eminent men of various prefectures and counties who had raised righteous forces made a blood oath; all were moved to indignant tears and accepted discipline awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu took the throne, Yizhang came south from Dezhou and Linqing and joined local officials and gentry who had raised loyalist forces in a blood oath. All wept with righteous indignation and pledged to await his command.

sentences.zh: 渡淮見可法，因建議：「山東、河北為江南籓蔽，若無山東、河北，是無中原、江北，無中原、江北，區區江南，豈能自守耶？

translations.literal: Crossing the Huai he met Kefa and therefore proposed: "Shandong and Hebei are the screen and shield of Jiangnan; without Shandong and Hebei, there is no central plains or north of the river; without the central plains and north of the river, how can the narrow Jiangnan defend itself?
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Huai he met Shi Kefa and urged: "Shandong and Hebei are Jiangnan's shield. Without them there is no central plains or territory north of the Yangzi. Without the central plains and the north, how can the Yangzi delta alone defend itself?

sentences.zh: 今宜於河南北、山東，設三大鎮，仿唐節度使、宋經制招討使之制，以大臣文武兼資者為之。

translations.literal: Now one should establish three great commands north of the Yellow River and in Shandong, following the Tang military commissioner and Song pacification commissioner systems, with great ministers possessing both civil and military capacity to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Establish three great commands north of the Yellow River and in Shandong, modeled on the Tang military commissioners and Song pacification commissioners, and place them under ministers skilled in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 寬其文法，使自為戰守，而閣部大治兵，居中馭之。

translations.literal: Relax bureaucratic restrictions on them, let them conduct their own warfare and defense, while the Grand Secretariat and ministries greatly organize troops and control them from the center.
translations.idiomatic: Give them broad autonomy in war and defense while the central government organizes the main armies and directs them from the capital.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「北方人心向順，宜及時撫為我用，否則忠者不能支，黠者反戈相向矣。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The hearts of the northern people incline toward submission; one should promptly win them for our use, otherwise the loyal cannot hold out and the cunning will turn their blades against us.
translations.idiomatic: " He also warned: "The people of the north still incline toward the dynasty. Win them now, or the loyal will not hold out and the cunning will turn their blades against us."

sentences.zh: 」前後奏記百數十。

translations.literal: " Before and after he submitted more than a hundred memorials and letters.
translations.idiomatic: " In all he submitted more than a hundred memorials and letters.

sentences.zh: 而馬士英專政，貨鬻官爵，用逆黨阮大鋮為兵部尚書，競立門戶，斥忠讜之士，君臣日夜酣樂。

translations.literal: But Ma Shiying monopolized government, sold offices and ranks for profit, employed the traitor faction's Ruan Dacheng as Minister of War, vied to establish factions, expelled loyal and forthright men, and ruler and ministers nightly reveled in pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Ma Shiying monopolized power, sold offices for profit, appointed the traitor Ruan Dacheng Minister of War, encouraged factional strife, expelled loyal critics, and ruler and ministers caroused day and night.

sentences.zh: 左良玉、高傑、劉澤清等各擁兵跋扈，莫能製。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu, Gao Jie, Liu Zeqing, and others each held troops and acted overbearingly; none could control them.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu, Gao Jie, Liu Zeqing, and other commanders each held private armies and defied control.

sentences.zh: 以樟知事不可為，憤鬱成疾，辭去。

translations.literal: Yizhang knew affairs could not be accomplished, fell ill from indignant depression, and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that nothing could be accomplished, Yizhang fell ill with grief and indignation and resigned.

sentences.zh: 可法仍舉以樟為兵部職方司主事，經理開、歸。

translations.literal: Kefa still recommended Yizhang as secretary in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War, to manage Kaifeng and Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa nevertheless appointed him secretary in the Bureau of Operations to manage affairs at Kaifeng and Guide.

sentences.zh: 未幾，揚州破，可法死，南都相繼潰。

translations.literal: Before long Yangzhou fell, Kefa died, and the southern capital collapsed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yangzhou fell, Shi Kefa died, and the southern capital collapsed in turn.

sentences.zh: 以樟遂與以棻遯跡寶應之葭湖，買田數十畝，躬耕自給。

translations.literal: Yizhang then with Yifen hid their traces at Jiahu in Baoying, bought several tens of mu of fields, and personally farmed to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhang then withdrew with Yifen to Jiahu in Baoying, bought several dozen mu of land, and supported himself by farming.

sentences.zh: 清初，召用勝國諸臣，以樟年才三十七，朝貴致書勸駕，不應。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing, surviving ministers of the previous dynasty were summoned to office; Yizhang was only thirty-seven, and court grandees sent letters urging him to take office—he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing, former Ming officials were summoned to serve. Yizhang was only thirty-seven, and court grandees wrote urging him to take office, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 自築忍冬軒，日與張★M9、孫爾靜講學其中，四方之士，若閻爾梅、王猷定、劉純學、崔干城、僧松隱暨其鄉人王世德父子，時時過以樟劇飲，慷慨激昂，繼以涕泣。

translations.literal: He built for himself the Honeysuckle Studio, daily lecturing therein with Zhang [character corrupted in text] and Sun Erjing; scholars from the four quarters, such as Yan Ermei, Wang Youding, Liu Chunxue, Cui Gancheng, the monk Songyin, and his fellow townsman Wang Shide and his sons, often visited Yizhang for heavy drinking, passionate and stirring, followed by weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Honeysuckle Studio and lectured there daily with Zhang Eryu and Sun Erjing. Scholars from far and wide—Yan Ermei, Wang Youding, Liu Chunxue, Cui Gancheng, the monk Songyin, and his fellow townsman Wang Shide and his sons—often visited for long drinking sessions, rising to passionate exhortation and ending in tears.

sentences.zh: 晚年偕喬出塵、陳鈺、硃克生、劉中柱結文字社。

translations.literal: In his later years, together with Qiao Chuchen, Chen Yu, Zhu Kesheng, and Liu Zhongzhu, he formed a literary society.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he joined Qiao Chuchen, Chen Yu, Zhu Kesheng, and Liu Zhongzhu in forming a literary society.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年七月十五日，端坐作論學數百言，擲筆而卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month of the fourth year of Kangxi, sitting upright he composed several hundred words on learning, cast down his brush, and died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month in the fourth year of Kangxi, he sat upright, composed several hundred words on learning, set down his brush, and died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 世德之子潔、源，集其理學、經濟諸書及詩、古文合為一編，曰梁鷦林先生全書，今傳世者，惟卬否詩集而已。

translations.literal: Shide's sons Jie and Yuan collected his books on Neo-Confucian learning, statecraft, poetry, and ancient prose into one compilation, titled The Complete Works of Master Liang Jiaolao; what survives today is only the Collection of Affirmation and Denial in verse.
translations.idiomatic: Shide's sons Jie and Yuan collected his works on philosophy, statecraft, poetry, and prose into one edition titled The Complete Works of Master Liang Jiaolao. Only his Collection of Affirmation and Denial in verse survives today.

sentences.zh: 世德，字克承，自號霜皋，北平人。

translations.literal: Shide, courtesy name Kecheng, style name Shuanggao, was a native of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shide, whose courtesy name was Kecheng and who styled himself Shuanggao, came from Beiping.

sentences.zh: 少襲錦衣衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In youth he inherited the post of assistant commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he inherited the post of assistant commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 北部陷，拔刀將引決，為僕所奪，妻魏已率婦女赴井死，遂易僧服，與以樟偕隱。

translations.literal: When the northern regions fell, he drew his sword intending to kill himself, but a servant seized it; his wife Wei had already led the women to throw themselves into a well and die; he then changed to monk's garb and went into seclusion with Yizhang.
translations.idiomatic: When the north fell he drew his sword to kill himself, but a servant wrested it away. His wife Wei had already led the women of the household to drown themselves in a well. He then donned monk's robes and withdrew into seclusion with Liang Yizhang.

sentences.zh: 嘗憤野史誣罔，不可傳信後世，欷歔扼腕，作崇禎遺錄一卷，自序之，康熙間修明史，有司錄其副本上史館。

translations.literal: Once, indignant that unofficial histories slandered and deceived and could not be trusted by posterity, he sighed and wrung his hands, composed one scroll of the Chongzhen Posthumous Record with his own preface; during the Kangxi compilation of the History of Ming, the authorities copied his manuscript and submitted it to the historiography office.
translations.idiomatic: Indignant that unreliable unofficial histories would mislead posterity, he sighed and wrung his hands and wrote a scroll of the Chongzhen Posthumous Record with his own preface. During the Kangxi compilation of the History of Ming, officials copied his manuscript and submitted it to the historiography office.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，卒，年八十有一。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi he died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 子源，以手藁殉葬。

translations.literal: His son Yuan buried his handwritten drafts with him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan had his handwritten drafts buried with him.

sentences.zh: 閻爾梅，字用卿，號古古，沛縣人。

translations.literal: Yan Ermei, courtesy name Yongqing, style name Gugu, was a native of Pei County.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ermei, whose courtesy name was Yongqing and style name Gugu, came from Pei County.

sentences.zh: 崇禎庚午舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the gengwu year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the gengwu year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷北京，爾梅上書請兵北伐，並儘散家財，結死士，為前驅。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng took Beijing, Ermei submitted a letter requesting troops for a northern expedition, and completely dispersed his family wealth, gathering dare-to-die men to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng seized Beijing, Ermei petitioned for a northern expedition, spent his entire family fortune, and gathered dare-to-die followers to serve as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 自成黨武愫至沛，屢使招爾梅，以碎牒大罵下獄，愫敗，乃免。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng's follower Wu Su arrived at Pei and repeatedly sent envoys to recruit Ermei; he tore the summons to pieces and cursed loudly, and was thrown into prison; when Su was defeated, he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's follower Wu Su came to Pei and repeatedly tried to recruit him. Ermei tore up the summons, cursed him loudly, and was thrown into prison. When Su was defeated, Ermei was released.

sentences.zh: 赴史可法之聘，參軍事，首勸渡河复山東，不聽。

translations.literal: He answered Shi Kefa's invitation, joined military affairs, and first urged crossing the river to recover Shandong—not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted Shi Kefa's invitation to join his staff and urged him first of all to cross the river and recover Shandong, but Kefa would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時高傑為許定國所殺，河南大亂，爾梅又說可法西行鎮撫之。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Jie was killed by Xu Dingguo and Henan fell into great disorder; Ermei again urged Kefa to go west and pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie had just been killed by Xu Dingguo and Henan was in chaos. Ermei again urged Kefa to go west and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 傑部將約束待命，可法為設提督統其眾，而自退保揚州。

translations.literal: Jie's subordinate generals were disciplined awaiting orders; Kefa established a regional commander to command their forces, and himself withdrew to defend Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie's subordinates were disciplined and awaiting orders. Kefa appointed a regional commander to lead them, while he himself withdrew to defend Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 爾梅力阻之，請開幕府徐州，號召河南北義勇，得以一成一旅規畫中原。

translations.literal: Ermei strenuously opposed this, requesting to open a headquarters at Xuzhou, summon righteous volunteers north and south of the Yellow River, and with even a single regiment plan for the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei strenuously opposed this and urged opening a headquarters at Xuzhou to rally loyal volunteers north and south of the Yellow River, so that even a single regiment might be used to plan the reconquest of the central plains.

sentences.zh: 又請空名告身數百紙，乘時布發，視忠義為鼓勵，俾逋寇叛帥不得以逾時渙散，少有睥睨。

translations.literal: He also requested several hundred blank commissions, to be distributed in timely fashion, treating loyalty and righteousness as encouragement, so that fleeing bandits and rebel commanders could not take advantage of delay to disperse and cast covetous eyes.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for several hundred blank commissions to distribute promptly as rewards for loyalty, so that scattered rebels and turncoat commanders could not exploit delay to regroup or grow bold.

sentences.zh: 策皆不行，遂貽以書而去。

translations.literal: None of these plans were adopted; he therefore sent a letter of parting and left.
translations.idiomatic: None of these plans was adopted, so he sent a letter of farewell and departed.

sentences.zh: 及可法殉節，爾梅走淮安，就劉澤清、田仰，畫戰守策，復不聽。

translations.literal: When Kefa died loyal to his post, Ermei fled to Huai'an, approached Liu Zeqing and Tian Yang, and outlined strategies of war and defense—again not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Kefa died defending his post, Ermei fled to Huai'an and presented war plans to Liu Zeqing and Tian Yang, but again they would not listen.

sentences.zh: 師入淮，爾梅率河北壯士伏城外，眾懼阻，羽士陶萬明特庇之。

translations.literal: When the army entered the Huai region, Ermei led stalwart men from Hebei to lie in ambush outside the city; the crowd feared obstruction; the Daoist Tao Wanming especially sheltered him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing forces entered the Huai region, Ermei led Hebei stalwarts to lie in ambush outside the city. Others feared the attempt would fail, but the Daoist Tao Wanming sheltered him.

sentences.zh: 巡撫趙福星以書招，爾梅痛哭謝之。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Zhao Fuxing summoned him by letter; Ermei wept and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhao Fuxing summoned him by letter. Ermei wept and refused.

sentences.zh: 乃散其眾，遁海上，祝髮，稱蹈東和尚。

translations.literal: He then dispersed his followers, fled to the sea, tonsured his head, and called himself the Monk Daodong.
translations.idiomatic: He dispersed his followers, fled to the coast, shaved his head, and took the monastic name Monk Daodong.

sentences.zh: 复走山東，聯絡四方魁傑，謀再舉。

translations.literal: Again he went to Shandong, contacted outstanding men of the four quarters, and plotted another rising.
translations.idiomatic: He went again to Shandong, contacted outstanding men throughout the realm, and plotted another uprising.

sentences.zh: 又至河南，至京師，以山東事發被捕，下濟南獄，脫走還沛。

translations.literal: He also went to Henan and to the capital; because the Shandong affair was exposed he was arrested, sent to prison in Jinan, escaped, and returned to Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to Henan and Beijing as well. When the Shandong plot was exposed he was arrested and imprisoned in Jinan, but escaped and returned to Pei.

sentences.zh: 名捕急，弟爾羹、侄禦九皆就逮，妻、妾同自縊。

translations.literal: Wanted posters were urgent; his younger brother Er'geng and nephew Yujiu were both arrested; his wife and concubine hanged themselves together.
translations.idiomatic: The hunt for him intensified. His younger brother Er'geng and nephew Yujiu were arrested, and his wife and concubine hanged themselves together.

sentences.zh: 爾梅乃託死夜遁，變名翁深，字藏若，歷遊楚、蜀、秦、晉九省。

translations.literal: Ermei then feigned death and fled by night, changed his name to Weng Shen, courtesy name Cangruo, and traveled through the nine provinces of Chu, Shu, Qin, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei then feigned death and fled by night under the name Weng Shen, courtesy name Cangruo, traveling through Chu, Shu, Qin, Jin, and other provinces.

sentences.zh: 過關中，與王弘撰等往還。

translations.literal: Passing through Guanzhong, he associated with Wang Hongzhuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Guanzhong, he associated with Wang Hongzhuan and others.

sentences.zh: 北至榆林，從寧夏入蘭州。

translations.literal: North to Yulin, from Ningxia into Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went north to Yulin and from Ningxia entered Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 凡十年，獄解，始還。

translations.literal: In all ten years the case was cleared, and only then did he return.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years the case against him was dropped, and he returned home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為仇家所攀，復出亡，龔鼎孳救之，得免。

translations.literal: Before long, implicated by an enemy family, he fled again; Gong Dingzi rescued him and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an enemy family implicated him and he fled again. Gong Dingzi intervened and saved him.

sentences.zh: 北謁思陵，又東出榆關。

translations.literal: North he paid homage at Siling, then eastward out through Yuguan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled north to pay homage at the Chongzhen Emperor's tomb, then east through Yuguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 還京，會顧炎武，复遊塞外。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he met Gu Yanwu, and again traveled beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital he met Gu Yanwu, then traveled again beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 至太原，訪傅山，結歲寒之盟。

translations.literal: Reaching Taiyuan, he visited Fu Shan and formed a covenant of winter friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan he visited Fu Shan and formed with him a covenant of steadfast friendship.

sentences.zh: 爾梅久奔走，歷艱險，不少阻。

translations.literal: Ermei long rushed about, experienced dangers, and was little deterred.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei wandered for years through hardship and danger, scarcely deterred.

sentences.zh: 後見大勢已去，知不可為，乃還沛。

translations.literal: Later, seeing the great trend had passed, knowing nothing could be done, he returned to Pei.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw that the cause was truly lost, he knew nothing more could be done and returned to Pei.

sentences.zh: 寄於酒，醉則罵座。

translations.literal: He entrusted himself to wine; when drunk he cursed those at table.
translations.idiomatic: He took refuge in wine and, when drunk, cursed those seated with him.

sentences.zh: 常慨然曰：「吾先世未有仕者，國亡，破家為報仇，天下震動。

translations.literal: He often said with emotion: "In my forebears none ever held office; when the state fell I ruined my family to avenge it, and the realm was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: He often said with emotion: "No one in my family had ever held office. When the dynasty fell I ruined my household to avenge it, and the realm trembled.

sentences.zh: 事雖終不成，疾風勁草，布衣之雄足矣！

translations.literal: Though the affair ultimately did not succeed, stern grass in a fierce wind—a hero in plain cloth is enough!
translations.idiomatic: Though we failed in the end, to stand firm in the storm—that is hero enough for a man in plain cloth!

sentences.zh: 」遂高歌起舞。

translations.literal: " He then sang loudly and danced.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he sang loudly and danced.

sentences.zh: 泣數行下。

translations.literal: Tears streamed down several lines.
translations.idiomatic: Tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 居數歲卒。

translations.literal: After several years' residence he died.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died.

sentences.zh: 年七十有七。

translations.literal: Aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-seven years old.

sentences.zh: 爾梅博學善詩，有白耷山人集。

translations.literal: Ermei was broadly learned and skilled in poetry; he has the Collected Works of the White-Coated Mountain Man.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei was broadly learned and skilled in poetry. His Collected Works of the White-Coated Mountain Man survives.

sentences.zh: 萬壽祺，字介若，世稱年少先生，徐州人。

translations.literal: Wan Shouqi, courtesy name Jieruo, commonly called Master Nianshao, was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Shouqi, whose courtesy name was Jieruo and who was commonly called Master Nianshao, came from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 與爾梅同郡，又同歲生，同舉鄉試，志節皆

translations.literal: With Ermei he was of the same prefecture, born in the same year, passed the provincial examination together, and in integrity and purpose were alike;
translations.idiomatic: He was from the same prefecture as Ermei, born in the same year and passing the provincial examination in the same year. They shared the same integrity and purpose,

sentences.zh: 同，既同舉事。

translations.literal: and likewise joined in raising the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: and they joined together in raising the loyalist cause.

sentences.zh: 南都破，江以南義師云起。

translations.literal: When the southern capital fell, righteous armies south of the river rose like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern capital fell, loyalist armies rose like clouds south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 沈自炳、戴之俊、錢邦芑起陳湖，黃家瑞、陳子龍起泖，吳易起笠澤，皆與會師，謀恢復。

translations.literal: Shen Zibing, Dai Zhijun, and Qian Bangji rose at Chenhu; Huang Jiarui and Chen Zilong rose at Mao; Wu Yi rose at Lizhe—all joined forces and plotted restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zibing, Dai Zhijun, and Qian Bangji rose at Chenhu; Huang Jiarui and Chen Zilong at Mao; Wu Yi at Lizhe. Shouqi joined their united forces to plan restoration.

sentences.zh: 兵潰，壽祺被執，不屈，將及難，有陰救之者，囚系月餘，得脫。

translations.literal: The army collapsed; Shouqi was captured and did not submit; about to meet disaster, someone secretly rescued him; imprisoned for more than a month, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the army collapsed he was captured but refused to submit. On the verge of execution he was secretly rescued, imprisoned for more than a month, and then escaped.

sentences.zh: 乃渡江歸隱，築室浦西，妻徐、子睿，灌園以自給。

translations.literal: He then crossed the river to live in seclusion, built a house west of the Pu, with his wife Xu and son Rui, and supported himself by gardening.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi to live in seclusion, built a house west of the Pu River, and supported his wife Xu and son Rui by tending a garden.

sentences.zh: 髡首被僧衣，自稱明志道人、沙門慧壽，而飲酒食肉如故。

translations.literal: He shaved his head and wore monk's robes, calling himself the Daoist Mingzhi and the monk Huishou, yet drank wine and ate meat as before.
translations.idiomatic: He shaved his head and wore monk's robes, calling himself the Daoist Mingzhi and the monk Huishou, yet continued to drink wine and eat meat as before.

sentences.zh: 時渡江而南，訪知舊，吊故壘。

translations.literal: From time to time he crossed south of the river, visited old acquaintances, and mourned at former battle sites.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time he crossed south of the Yangzi to visit old friends and mourn at former battle sites.

sentences.zh: 遺民故老過淮陰者，亦輒造草堂，流連歌哭，或淹留旬月。

translations.literal: Surviving subjects and old men passing through Huaiyin also often came to his thatched hall, lingering in song and weeping, sometimes staying a month or more.
translations.idiomatic: Surviving loyalists and old friends passing through Huaiyin also came to his thatched hall, lingering in song and tears, sometimes staying for a month or more.

sentences.zh: 雖隱居，固未嘗一日忘世也。

translations.literal: Though in seclusion, he never for a single day forgot the world.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lived in seclusion, he never for a single day forgot the world.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 壽祺善詩、文、書、畫，旁及琴、劍、棋、曲、雕刻、刺繡，亦靡弗工妙。

translations.literal: Shouqi was skilled in poetry, prose, calligraphy, and painting; extending to the zither, sword, chess, drama, carving, and embroidery—none in which he was not masterfully accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqi excelled in poetry, prose, calligraphy, and painting, and was equally accomplished in the zither, swordplay, chess, drama, carving, and embroidery.

sentences.zh: 爾梅論有明一代書，推為第一。

translations.literal: Ermei, discussing calligraphy of the entire Ming, ranked him first.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei, surveying Ming calligraphy as a whole, ranked him first.

sentences.zh: 著有隰西草堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Collection of the Xixi Thatched Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Collection of the Xixi Thatched Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，爾梅、壽祺同謀舉事，一起江北，一起江南，先後相呼應。

translations.literal: At first Ermei and Shouqi together plotted to raise the cause—one rising north of the river, one south, responding to each other in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ermei and Shouqi plotted together to raise the loyalist cause—one in the north, one in the south, coordinating their efforts.

sentences.zh: 及事敗，爾梅出走，思得一當。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, Ermei fled, thinking to win one decisive stroke.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause failed, Ermei fled, still hoping for one decisive stroke.

sentences.zh: 壽祺留江、淮觀世變，不幸先死。

translations.literal: Shouqi remained on the Jiang and Huai to observe the changes of the age, but unfortunately died first.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqi remained in the Jiang-Huai region to watch how events unfolded, but unfortunately died first.

sentences.zh: 爾梅獨奔走三十餘年，亦終無所就。

translations.literal: Ermei alone rushed about for more than thirty years, yet ultimately achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei wandered alone for more than thirty years, yet ultimately achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 後世稱「徐州二遺民」，常為之太息雲。

translations.literal: Later ages call them "the two surviving subjects of Xuzhou," and often sigh deeply over them.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations called them "the two surviving subjects of Xuzhou," and often sighed deeply over their fate.

sentences.zh: 鄭與僑，字惠人，號確菴，濟寧人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yiqiao, courtesy name Huiren, style name Que'an, was a native of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yiqiao, whose courtesy name was Huiren and style name Que'an, came from Jining.

sentences.zh: 五歲父歿，母張以祖遺田讓之仲，獨取遺書一篋授僑，曰：「兒讀此，可飽也！

translations.literal: At five his father died; his mother Zhang gave the ancestral fields to his second uncle, and alone took one basket of inherited books and gave them to Yiqiao, saying: "My son, read these and you may be fed!
translations.idiomatic: When he was five his father died. His mother Zhang gave the ancestral fields to his uncle and kept only one basket of inherited books for Yiqiao, saying, "My son, read these and you will never go hungry!

sentences.zh: 」與僑發奮力學，崇禎丙子舉於鄉。

translations.literal: " Yiqiao applied himself vigorously to study, and in the bingzi year of Chongzhen passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: " Yiqiao applied himself vigorously to his studies and passed the provincial examination in the bingzi year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 時流寇充斥山左，與僑以濟寧為漕艘咽喉地，倡義與城守張世臣、舉人孟瑄並力殺賊，城賴以完。

translations.literal: At that time roaming bandits filled Shandong; Yiqiao, because Jining was the throat of the grain-transport fleet, raised the righteous cause with city defender Zhang Shichen and provincial graduate Meng Xuan, together killing bandits, and the city was preserved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits then filled Shandong. Because Jining was the vital junction of the grain-transport route, Yiqiao raised a loyalist force with Zhang Shichen, defender of the city, and the graduate Meng Xuan. Together they killed the rebels and preserved the city.

sentences.zh: 有賊郭升者，將至濟寧州，吏議迎款，囑與僑草表，力拒乃止。

translations.literal: There was a bandit Guo Sheng about to reach Jining Prefecture; officials discussed welcoming surrender and asked Yiqiao to draft the submission document; he strenuously refused and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Guo Sheng was about to reach Jining, officials discussed surrender and asked Yiqiao to draft the submission. He refused strenuously and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及賊至，與僑率鄉人殲之，遂徙家淮陽。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, Yiqiao led the villagers to annihilate them, then moved his family to Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, Yiqiao led the villagers to destroy them, then moved his family to Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 史可法方開府淮上，聞與僑名，奏為儀真令，而吏部以其前守濟寧功，改除揚州府推官。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa had just opened his headquarters on the Huai; hearing Yiqiao's reputation, he memorialized to appoint him magistrate of Yizhen, but the Ministry of Personnel, because of his former merit defending Jining, changed the appointment to investigating censor of Yangzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa had just established his headquarters on the Huai. Hearing of Yiqiao's reputation, he recommended him as magistrate of Yizhen, but the Ministry of Personnel, honoring his defense of Jining, appointed him investigating censor of Yangzhou Prefecture instead.

sentences.zh: 揚州為興平伯高傑列籓地，其將卒多驕橫，稍不當意，抽刀剚人，與僑悉裁之以法。

translations.literal: Yangzhou was the fief territory of the Xingping Earl Gao Jie; his officers and soldiers were mostly arrogant and overbearing—slightly displeased, they drew knives and stabbed people; Yiqiao judged them all by law.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou was the domain of the Xingping Earl Gao Jie. His soldiers were arrogant and would draw their swords at the slightest provocation. Yiqiao punished every offender according to law.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史何綸薦以推官監江、海軍，駐通州。

translations.literal: Touring censor He Lun recommended him as investigating censor to supervise river and sea forces, stationed at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor He Lun recommended him to supervise river and coastal forces as investigating censor, stationed at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 江南失守，與僑奉母之武林，總督張存仁、經略洪承疇奇其才，欲官之，皆謝不起。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was lost, Yiqiao took his mother to Wulin; Governor-General Zhang Cunren and frontier commissioner Hong Chengchou marveled at his talent and wished to give him office—he declined all and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan fell, Yiqiao took his mother to Hangzhou. Governor-General Zhang Cunren and Frontier Commissioner Hong Chengchou admired his talent and wished to appoint him, but he declined every offer.

sentences.zh: 後歸濟上，立社教授生徒，絕口不談時事。

translations.literal: Later he returned to Jining, established a school to teach students, and never spoke of current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to Jining, founded a school to teach students, and never spoke of current affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘗遍遊秦、晉、川、蜀、荊、楚、吳、越諸勝，著有確菴稿、丹照集、爭光集、濟寧遺事、秦邊記要等書。

translations.literal: Once he traveled widely through the scenic places of Qin, Jin, Sichuan, Shu, Jing, Chu, Wu, and Yue; he authored the Que'an Drafts, Danzhao Collection, Zhengguang Collection, Jining Reminiscences, Records of the Qin Frontier, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled widely through Qin, Jin, Sichuan, Jing, Chu, Wu, Yue, and other regions. He left works including the Que'an Drafts, Danzhao Collection, Zhengguang Collection, Jining Reminiscences, and Records of the Qin Frontier.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十有四。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 自為壙志。

translations.literal: He composed his own tomb inscription.
translations.idiomatic: He composed his own tomb inscription.

sentences.zh: 曹元方，字介皇，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Cao Yuanfang, courtesy name Jiehuang, was a native of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuanfang, whose courtesy name was Jiehuang, came from Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 父履泰，明兵部侍郎，以忠直著。

translations.literal: His father Lütai was a vice minister of war in the Ming, renowned for loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lütai had been a vice minister of war in the Ming and was renowned for loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 元方，崇禎癸未進士，南京建號，授常熟知縣。

translations.literal: Yuanfang, a jinshi in the guiwei year of Chongzhen, when Nanjing established its reign was appointed magistrate of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang became a jinshi in the guiwei year of Chongzhen. When Nanjing proclaimed its regime, he was appointed magistrate of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 時大學士馬士英擅國政，有薦元方署職方司事者，士英亦藉元方名，冀往謁附己，元方訖不往。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Secretary Ma Shiying monopolized state affairs; someone recommended Yuanfang to serve in the Bureau of Operations; Shiying also wished to use Yuanfang's name, hoping he would come to pay court and attach himself—Yuanfang never went.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ma Shiying then monopolized the government. Someone recommended Yuanfang for a post in the Bureau of Operations, and Shiying hoped Yuanfang would come pay court and join his faction. Yuanfang never went.

sentences.zh: 上疏言原遵定制補外吏，語侵士英，士英怒，卒與令常熟。

translations.literal: He memorialized saying he wished to follow established regulations and take an outer-office post; his words impugned Shiying; Shiying was angry, and in the end let him have the magistracy of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that he wished to follow regulations and take an outer-office post, implicating Shiying in the process. Shiying was furious but in the end allowed him to remain magistrate of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 常熟為吳中煩劇邑最，當金陵草創，所在兵與民交狃無寧晷。

translations.literal: Changshu was the most troublesome and demanding county in Wu; when Jinling was newly founded, everywhere soldiers and people clashed without a moment's peace.
translations.idiomatic: Changshu was the most difficult county in the Wu region. While Nanjing was being established, soldiers and civilians clashed everywhere without respite.

sentences.zh: 元方措兵餉，惜民力，俱帖然，邑稱治。

translations.literal: Yuanfang arranged military supplies, cherished the people's strength, and all were settled; the county was called well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang arranged military supplies, spared the people's strength, and brought order. The county was said to be well governed.

sentences.zh: 金陵敗，棄官歸，履泰先獲譴謫戍，亦適歸。

translations.literal: When Jinling fell, he abandoned office and returned; Lütai had earlier been punished and banished to frontier service, and also happened to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell he resigned and returned home. Lütai had already been punished and banished to frontier service and happened to return at the same time.

sentences.zh: 父子相謂，於義不可晏然以居。

translations.literal: Father and son said to each other that in righteousness they could not live at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son agreed that in honor they could not live at ease.

sentences.zh: 元方先變姓名，間道入閩，至建寧，謁唐王。

translations.literal: Yuanfang first changed his name, took bypaths into Fujian, reached Jianning, and paid audience to the Tang Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang changed his name, traveled by secret routes into Fujian, reached Jianning, and presented himself to the Tang Prince.

sentences.zh: 即授吏部文選司主事，晉驗封司郎中。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed secretary in the Bureau of Appointments of the Ministry of Personnel, and promoted to director in the Bureau of Seals.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed secretary in the Bureau of Appointments and later promoted to director in the Bureau of Seals.

sentences.zh: 頃之，履泰亦由海道至，即授太常卿，晉兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long Lütai also arrived by sea route and was immediately appointed Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted to vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lütai arrived by sea and was appointed Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 父子俱以忠義激發，間關來，一時咸偉之。

translations.literal: Father and son both, stirred by loyalty and righteousness, came by perilous routes, and for a time all admired them.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son, stirred by loyalty and righteousness, had made the perilous journey together, and for a time all admired them.

sentences.zh: 當是時，鄭芝龍久以桀寇內附，崇其秩號，姑息為養驕，至是益甚，志叵測。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Zhilong had long submitted as a fierce pirate, was elevated in rank and title, and was indulgently nurtured into arrogance; by now this was even worse, and his intentions were hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhilong had long since submitted as a former pirate and been elevated in rank. The court had indulged him until he grew arrogant, and by now his intentions were impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 元方抗疏，自請出視江上師，閱封守，欲從外為重內計。

translations.literal: Yuanfang submitted a forceful memorial, requesting on his own to go out and inspect the forces on the river, review defenses, wishing from outside to strengthen the plan within.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang submitted a forceful memorial volunteering to inspect the river forces and review defenses, hoping to strengthen the court's position from without.

sentences.zh: 得召對，加御史銜，賜白金，揮涕以行。

translations.literal: He obtained an imperial audience, was given the censor's title, bestowed white silver, and set out wiping away tears.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an audience, given the title of censor, presented with silver, and set out wiping away tears.

sentences.zh: 至浦城，則江上潰兵接踵狼狽下，元方倉卒走，計後圖。

translations.literal: Reaching Pucheng, routed soldiers on the river came down one after another in disarray; Yuanfang fled in haste, planning for later.
translations.idiomatic: At Pucheng he found routed soldiers streaming down the river in disorder. Yuanfang fled in haste to plan his next move.

sentences.zh: 履泰從唐王趨贛州，遇兵，投身崖石下，絕复甦。

translations.literal: Lütai followed the Tang Prince toward Ganzhou, encountered troops, threw himself beneath a cliff, ceased breathing and revived.
translations.idiomatic: Lütai followed the Tang Prince toward Ganzhou, was caught in fighting, and threw himself from a cliff. He stopped breathing and then revived.

sentences.zh: 舁至僧舍，展轉至浦城，父子得相見。

translations.literal: Carried to a monk's dwelling, he was transferred by stages to Pucheng, and father and son were able to meet.
translations.idiomatic: He was carried to a monastery and then conveyed in stages to Pucheng, where father and son were reunited.

sentences.zh: 履泰疾甚，先歸，旋卒於家。

translations.literal: Lütai's illness was severe; he returned first and soon died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Lütai fell gravely ill, returned home first, and soon died there.

sentences.zh: 元方聞，乃亟歸，微服挈母及妻子行，寄食旅舍中。

translations.literal: Yuanfang heard and hurried home, in plain dress taking his mother and wife and children on the road, lodging and eating in inns.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news Yuanfang hurried home in plain dress with his mother, wife, and children, lodging in inns along the way.

sentences.zh: 久之，事稍定，卜居硤石村，築草堂，自號耘庵。

translations.literal: After a long while affairs settled somewhat; he chose residence at Jiaoshi Village, built a thatched hall, and styled himself the Plowing Hermitage.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs had settled somewhat, he chose a home at Jiaoshi Village, built a thatched hall, and styled himself the Plowing Hermitage.

sentences.zh: 以老卒，年八十有二。

translations.literal: He died of old age, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died of old age at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 莊元辰，字起貞，晚字頑菴，鄞人，學者稱漢曉先生。

translations.literal: Zhuang Yuanchen, courtesy name Qizhen, late style name Wan'an, was a native of Yin; scholars called him Master Hanxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Yuanchen, whose courtesy name was Qizhen and whose later style name was Wan'an, came from Yin. Scholars called him Master Hanxiao.

sentences.zh: 賦性嚴凝，不隨人唯阿。

translations.literal: By nature stern and austere, he did not follow others in flattery.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and austere and would not follow others in flattery.

sentences.zh: 崇禎丁丑進士，授南京太常博士。

translations.literal: In the dingchou year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi and was appointed Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the dingchou year of Chongzhen and was appointed Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 甲申之變，一日七至中樞史可法之門，促以勤王，福王立，議推科臣，總憲劉宗周、掌科章正宸皆舉元辰為首，而馬士英密遣私人致意曰：「博士曷不持門下刺上謁相公？

translations.literal: At the disaster of jiashen, in one day he came seven times to the gate of Grand Secretary Shi Kefa to urge relief of the throne. When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, in discussions to recommend members of the Censorate, Grand Coordinator Liu Zongzhou and supervising censor Zhang Zhengchen both put Yuanchen first, but Ma Shiying secretly sent a private agent with a message saying: "Doctor, why not carry your visiting card and go up to pay respects to the Grand Secretary?
translations.idiomatic: At the jiashen disaster he visited Grand Secretary Shi Kefa's gate seven times in a single day to urge relief of the throne. When the Prince of Fu was enthroned and censorial posts were being discussed, Grand Coordinator Liu Zongzhou and supervising censor Zhang Zhengchen both ranked Yuanchen first. Ma Shiying secretly sent a private agent with a message: "Doctor, why not carry your visiting card and go pay your respects to the Grand Secretary?

sentences.zh: 掌科必無他屬。

translations.literal: The position of supervising censor would certainly have no other nominee."
translations.idiomatic: The post of supervising censor would surely have no other nominee."

sentences.zh: 」峻拒之。

translations.literal: He sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: He refused sternly.

sentences.zh: 中旨僅授刑部主事。

translations.literal: By palace edict he was granted only the post of principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: A palace edict appointed him only as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 已而阮大鋮欲興同文之獄，元辰曰：「禍將烈矣！

translations.literal: Before long Ruan Dacheng wished to raise the Tongwen case; Yuanchen said: "Disaster is about to blaze fiercely!
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ruan Dacheng sought to revive the Tongwen persecution. Yuanchen said, "Disaster is about to break out in full force!

sentences.zh: 」遽行，未幾而留都亡。

translations.literal: " He departed at once; before long the southern capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: " He left at once. Before long the southern capital fell.

sentences.zh: 錢肅樂之起事也，元辰破家輸餉，時降臣謝三賓為王之仁所脅，以餉自贖。

translations.literal: When Qian Sule raised the loyalist cause, Yuanchen ruined his family to supply funds. At that time the surrendered minister Xie Sanbin, coerced by Wang Zhiren, offered funds to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Sule raised the loyalist cause, Yuanchen ruined his family to supply funds. At that time the surrendered minister Xie Sanbin, coerced by Wang Zhiren, offered funds to buy his way back into favor.

sentences.zh: 及肅樂與之仁赴江上，三賓潛招兵，眾疑之。

translations.literal: When Sule and Zhiren went to the river front, Sanbin secretly recruited troops, and people grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When Sule and Zhiren went to the river front, Sanbin secretly recruited troops, and suspicion spread.

sentences.zh: 明經王家勤謂肅樂曰：「浙東沿海皆可以舟師達鹽官，倘彼乘風而渡，列城且立潰矣，非分兵留守不可。

translations.literal: The classics graduate Wang Jiaqin said to Sule: "Along the Zhedong coast fleet troops can reach Yanguan by boat. If they catch the wind and cross, the cities will promptly collapse. We must divide troops to garrison and hold."
translations.idiomatic: The classics graduate Wang Jiaqin said to Sule, "Along the Zhedong coast, naval forces can reach Yanguan by boat. If the enemy catches a favorable wind and crosses, the cities will collapse at once. We must detach troops to hold the rear."

sentences.zh: 」肅樂曰：「是無以易吾莊公者。

translations.literal: Sule said: "There is no one who could replace our Master Zhuang for this."
translations.idiomatic: Sule said, "There is no one who could replace our Master Zhuang for this task."

sentences.zh: 」於是共推元辰任城守事，分兵千人屬之，以四明驛為幕府，家勤及林時躍參其事。

translations.literal: Accordingly they jointly recommended Yuanchen to take charge of city defense, assigned him a thousand troops, and made the Siming post station the headquarters; Jiaqin and Lin Shiyue assisted in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: They then jointly recommended Yuanchen to take charge of the city's defense, assigned him a thousand troops, and made the Siming post station his headquarters, with Jiaqin and Lin Shiyue assisting him.

sentences.zh: 元辰日耀兵巡諸堞裡，人呼為「城門軍」，三賓不敢動。

translations.literal: Yuanchen daily displayed troops and patrolled the battlements; people called them the "City Gate Army," and Sanbin did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchen daily paraded troops and patrolled the battlements. People called them the "City Gate Army," and Sanbin did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 乃迎魯王於天台，鄞始解嚴。

translations.literal: Only then was the Prince of Lu welcomed at Tiantai, and Yin at last lifted martial law.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was the Prince of Lu welcomed at Tiantai, and Yin at last lifted martial law.

sentences.zh: 晉吏科都給事中，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel, then transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel and then transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「殿下大仇未雪，舉兵以來，將士宣勞於外，編氓殫藏於內，臥薪嘗之不遑，而數月來，頗安逸樂。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Your Highness's great vengeance remains unavenged. Since raising arms, officers and soldiers proclaim their labors abroad while the common people exhaust their stores at home—they have no leisure even for sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall—yet for several months now you have grown rather easeful and merry.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Your Highness's great vengeance remains unavenged. Since raising arms, officers and soldiers proclaim their labors abroad while the common people exhaust their stores at home. There has been no leisure even for sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall, yet for several months now you have grown rather easeful and merry.

sentences.zh: 釜魚幕燕，撫事增憂，則晏安何可懷也？

translations.literal: Like fish in a cauldron or swallows under a canopy, when I reflect on affairs my worry grows—how then can contentment at ease be cherished?
