translations.idiomatic: We are like fish in a cauldron or swallows under a canopy. When I reflect on affairs my worry only grows—how then can we cherish contentment and ease?

sentences.zh: 敵在門庭，朝不及夕，有深宮養優之心，安得有前席借箸之事，則蒙蔽何可滋也？

translations.literal: The enemy is at the gate; morning may not see evening. If there is a heart to nurture entertainers deep in the palace, how can there be the matter of moving forward one's mat and borrowing chopsticks? Then how can deception flourish?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is at the gate, and morning may not see evening. If the heart is set on nurturing entertainers deep in the palace, how can there be the matter of moving forward one's mat and borrowing chopsticks to plan strategy? Then how can deception be allowed to spread?

sentences.zh: 天下安危，託命將相，今左右之人，頗能內承色笑，則事權何可移也？

translations.literal: The safety and peril of the realm are entrusted to generals and ministers; yet those at your side can rather well receive your smiles within—and then how can authority remain where it belongs?
translations.idiomatic: The safety and peril of the realm are entrusted to generals and ministers, yet those at your side can all too easily win your smiles within the palace. How then can authority remain where it belongs?

sentences.zh: 五等崇封，有如探囊，有為昔時佐命元臣所不能得者，則恩膏何可濫也？

translations.literal: Enfeoffment of the five ranks is like reaching into a pouch; some receive what even founding ministers of old could not obtain—then how can grace and bounty be lavished so?
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffment of the five ranks is handed out like taking something from a pouch. Some receive honors that even founding ministers of old could not obtain—how then can grace and bounty be lavished so recklessly?

sentences.zh: 陛下試念兩都黍離麥秀之悲，則居處必不安；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would try to recall the grief of "Grain Ears" and "Wheat in Blossom" over the two capitals, your dwelling would surely be uneasy;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would recall the grief of "Grain Ears" and "Wheat in Blossom" over the two capitals, your dwelling would surely be uneasy;

sentences.zh: 試念孝陵、長陵銅駝荊棘之慘，則對越必不安；

translations.literal: try to recall the horror of bronze camels and brambles at Xiaoling and Changling, and your facing Heaven would surely be uneasy;
translations.idiomatic: if you would recall the horror of bronze camels and brambles at Xiaoling and Changling, your facing Heaven would surely be uneasy;

sentences.zh: 試念青宮二王之辱，則撫王子何以為情；

translations.literal: try to recall the disgrace of the Eastern Palace and the two princes, and what feeling could there be in embracing the princes?
translations.idiomatic: if you would recall the disgrace suffered by the Eastern Palace and the two princes, what feeling could there be in embracing the princes?

sentences.zh: 試念江乾將士列邦生民之困，則衣食可以俱廢。

translations.literal: try to recall the hardship of officers and soldiers on the river and the people of the realms, and then food and clothing may both be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: If you would recall the hardship of the officers and soldiers on the river and the people of the realm, then food and clothing may both be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgement was returned.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the court acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 已又言中旨用人之非，累有封駁，王不能用。

translations.literal: Subsequently he again spoke of the wrong in palace-edict appointments; repeatedly he submitted rebuttals, but the prince could not employ his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He then again criticized the improper use of palace edicts in appointments, repeatedly submitting rebuttals, but the prince would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 時三賓夤緣居要，而馬士英又至，元辰言：「士英不斬，國事必不可為！

translations.literal: At that time Sanbin had connived his way into important posts, and Ma Shiying also arrived. Yuanchen said: "Unless Shiying is executed, state affairs absolutely cannot be accomplished!
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sanbin had connived his way into important posts, and Ma Shiying also arrived. Yuanchen said, "Unless Shiying is executed, state affairs cannot possibly be saved!

sentences.zh: 」貽書同官黃宗羲、林時對云：「蕞爾氣象，似惟恐其不速盡者，區區憂憤，無事不痛心疾首，以致咳嗽纏綿，形容骨立。

translations.literal: He sent letters to colleagues Huang Zongxi and Lin Shidui saying: "This tiny realm's air is as though it fears only that it will not perish quickly enough. My petty worry and indignation leave nothing that does not pierce heart and head, until cough lingers on and my frame stands like bones alone.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to colleagues Huang Zongxi and Lin Shidui, saying, "This tiny realm seems to fear only that it will not perish quickly enough. My worry and indignation leave nothing that does not pierce heart and head, until my cough lingers on and my frame is reduced to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 原得以微罪，成其山野。

translations.literal: I wish by a minor fault to achieve my withdrawal to the mountains and wilds."
translations.idiomatic: I ask only to be allowed a minor fault so that I may withdraw to the mountains and wilds."

sentences.zh: 」遂乞休。

translations.literal: He then requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大兵東下，乃狂走深山中，朝夕野哭。

translations.literal: Before long the great army marched east; he then fled madly into deep mountains, weeping in the wild morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Qing army marched east. He fled madly into the deep mountains and wept in the wilderness morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 元辰故美鬚眉，顧盼落落，至是失其面目，巾服似頭陀，一日數徙，莫知所止，山中人亦不復識。

translations.literal: Yuanchen had formerly handsome beard and brows and a lofty bearing in his glance; by now he had lost his former face; cap and robes resembled a mendicant monk's; he moved several times in a day, and none knew where he stopped—nor did mountain people recognize him again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchen had once been handsome of beard and brow, with a lofty bearing in his glance. By now he had lost his former face; his cap and robes resembled a mendicant monk's. He moved several times in a day, and no one knew where he stopped—even the mountain people no longer recognized him.

sentences.zh: 忽有老婦呼其小字曰：「子非念四郎邪？

translations.literal: Suddenly an old woman called his childhood name, saying: "Are you not Niansilang?
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly an old woman called his childhood name, saying, "Are you not Niansilang?

sentences.zh: 」因歎曰：「吾晦跡未深，奈何？

translations.literal: " He sighed and said: "My concealment is not yet deep enough—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: " He sighed and said, "My concealment is not yet deep enough—what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 」順治四年，疽發背，戒勿藥，曰：「吾死已晚，然及今死猶可。

translations.literal: " In the fourth year of Shunzhi a carbuncle broke out on his back; he warned against medicine, saying: "My death is already late, yet to die even now may still do.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth year of Shunzhi a carbuncle broke out on his back. He forbade medicine, saying, "My death is already late, yet to die even now may still suffice.

sentences.zh: 」遂卒。

translations.literal: " He then died.
translations.idiomatic: " He then died.

sentences.zh: 王玉藻，字質夫，江都人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuzao, courtesy name Zhifu, was a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuzao, whose courtesy name was Zhifu, came from Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎癸未進士，授慈溪知縣。

translations.literal: In the guiwei year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the guiwei year of Chongzhen and was appointed magistrate of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 少詹項煜以從逆亡命，玉藻及慈民馮元飚均出其門，遂匿於馮氏。

translations.literal: Junior Guardian Xiang Yu fled as a fugitive for following the rebels; Yuzao and the Cixi native Feng Yuanbiao had both been his pupils, so Yuzao hid with the Feng family.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Guardian Xiang Yu fled as a fugitive for following the rebels. Yuzao and the Cixi native Feng Yuanbiao had both been his pupils, so Yuzao hid with the Feng family.

sentences.zh: 慈人斃煜於水，玉藻置不問。

translations.literal: Men of Cixi killed Yu by drowning; Yuzao let the matter alone.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Cixi drowned Yu, and Yuzao let the matter alone.

sentences.zh: 有明士習重闈誼，或以為過，玉藻曰：「吾豈能為向雄之待鍾會哉！

translations.literal: Ming scholar custom valued the bond of the examination hall; some considered this excessive. Yuzao said: "How could I act like Xiang Xiong waiting on Zhong Hui!
translations.idiomatic: Ming scholars valued the bond of the examination hall, and some considered this excessive. Yuzao said, "How could I act like Xiang Xiong waiting on Zhong Hui!

sentences.zh: 夫君臣之與師友，果孰重？

translations.literal: Between ruler and subject on the one hand and teacher and friend on the other—which is truly weightier?
translations.idiomatic: Between ruler and subject on the one hand and teacher and friend on the other—which is truly the weightier bond?

sentences.zh: 」聞者悚然。

translations.literal: " Those who heard were struck with awe.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who heard were struck with awe.

sentences.zh: 金陵破，魯王監國，玉藻乃與沈宸荃起兵，晉御史，仍行縣。

translations.literal: When Jinling fell and the Prince of Lu assumed regency, Yuzao raised troops with Shen Chenquan, was promoted to censor, and still performed county duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinling fell and the Prince of Lu assumed regency, Yuzao raised troops with Shen Chenquan, was promoted to censor, and continued to perform his county duties.

sentences.zh: 复募義勇，請赴江上自劾，略謂：「今恃以自保者，惟錢唐一江，待北兵渡江而後禦，曷若御之於未渡之先？

translations.literal: He again recruited volunteers and requested to go to the river front at his own initiative, saying in summary: "What we rely on for self-preservation now is only the Qiantang River. To wait until northern troops cross the river before defending—how does that compare with blocking them before they cross?
translations.idiomatic: He again recruited volunteers and asked to go to the river front on his own initiative, saying in summary, "What we rely on for self-preservation now is only the Qiantang River. To wait until northern troops cross the river before defending—how does that compare with blocking them before they cross?

sentences.zh: 臣原以身先之！

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to take the lead with his own body!"
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes to take the lead with his own body!"

sentences.zh: 」乃解縣事，以兵科都給事往軍前。

translations.literal: He then relinquished county affairs and went to the army as Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War.
translations.idiomatic: He then relinquished his county duties and went to the army as Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War.

sentences.zh: 時駐兵江上者，有方國安、王之仁、孫嘉績、熊汝霖、章正宸、鄭道謙、錢肅樂、沈光文、陳潛夫、黃宗羲，咸各自為軍，兵餉交訌，莫敢先進。

translations.literal: Those then encamped on the river included Fang Guo'an, Wang Zhiren, Sun Jiaji, Xiong Rulin, Zhang Zhengchen, Zheng Daoqian, Qian Sule, Shen Guangwen, Chen Qianfu, and Huang Zongxi—all maintained separate armies; funds and provisions clashed, and none dared advance first.
translations.idiomatic: Those then encamped on the river included Fang Guo'an, Wang Zhiren, Sun Jiaji, Xiong Rulin, Zhang Zhengchen, Zheng Daoqian, Qian Sule, Shen Guangwen, Chen Qianfu, and Huang Zongxi. Each maintained a separate army; funds and provisions clashed, and none dared advance first.

sentences.zh: 既不予玉藻以餉，复陳劃地分餉，又不聽，玉藻乃力請還朝。

translations.literal: When they neither gave Yuzao supplies nor listened to his proposal to divide territory and allot funds, Yuzao forcefully petitioned to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: When they neither gave Yuzao supplies nor listened to his proposal to divide territory and allot funds, Yuzao forcefully petitioned to return to court.

sentences.zh: 既入諫垣，上封事十餘，略謂：「北兵之可畏者在勇，而我軍之可慮者在怯，怯由於驕，兵驕由於將驕。

translations.literal: Once in the remonstrance office he submitted more than ten sealed memorials, saying in summary: "What makes northern troops fearsome is courage; what makes our army worrisome is timidity—and timidity comes from arrogance, and troop arrogance from general arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the remonstrance office he submitted more than ten sealed memorials, saying in summary, "What makes northern troops fearsome is courage; what makes our army worrisome is timidity. Timidity comes from arrogance, and troop arrogance from general arrogance.

sentences.zh: 今統兵之將，無汗馬之勞，輒博五等之封，安得不啟以驕心？

translations.literal: Generals commanding troops today, without labor of sweating horses, gamble for enfeoffment of the five ranks—how can this not awaken an arrogant heart?
translations.idiomatic: Generals commanding troops today, without the labor of sweating horses, gamble for enfeoffment of the five ranks—how can this fail to awaken an arrogant heart?

sentences.zh: 驕則畏戰，非稍加裁抑，恐無以戢其囂陵之氣。

translations.literal: Arrogance breeds fear of battle; unless they are somewhat restrained, I fear there will be no way to curb their overbearing air.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogance breeds fear of battle. Unless they are somewhat restrained, I fear there will be no way to curb their overbearing air.

sentences.zh: 」又謂：「宜用海師窺吳淞，以分杭州北兵之勢。

translations.literal: He also said: "Naval forces should be used to probe Wusong and divide the pressure of northern troops on Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Naval forces should be used to probe Wusong and divide the pressure of northern troops on Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又劉宗周、祁彪佳諸臣，宜加褒忠之典。

translations.literal: Ministers such as Liu Zongzhou and Qi Bujia should receive posthumous honors for loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers such as Liu Zongzhou and Qi Bujia should receive posthumous honors for loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」以是不為諸臣所喜，乃力求罷職。

translations.literal: Because of this he was not favored by the various ministers, and he strenuously sought to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he was not favored by the various ministers, and he strenuously sought to resign.

sentences.zh: 時元辰為太常，固乞留之，謂：「古人折檻旌直，今令直臣去國，豈國家之福！

translations.literal: At that time Yuanchen was Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and earnestly begged him to stay, saying: "The ancients broke the balustrade to honor the upright; now to let upright ministers leave the state—is that the realm's good fortune?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuanchen was Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and earnestly begged him to stay, saying, "The ancients broke the balustrade to honor the upright. Now to let upright ministers leave the state—is that the realm's good fortune?

sentences.zh: 」玉藻感其言，供職如初。

translations.literal: " Moved by his words, Yuzao resumed his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Moved by his words, Yuzao resumed his duties as before.

sentences.zh: 浙東再破，玉藻追魯王蹕，弗及，自投於池，水涸，不得死，乃以黃冠遯於剡溪。

translations.literal: When Zhedong fell again, Yuzao pursued the Prince of Lu's entourage but could not catch up; he threw himself into a pool, but the water was dry and he could not die; he then fled to Shan Creek wearing a Daoist cap.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhedong fell again, Yuzao pursued the Prince of Lu's entourage but could not catch up. He threw himself into a pool, but the water was dry and he could not die. He then fled to Shan Creek wearing a Daoist cap.

sentences.zh: 資糧俱盡，採野葛為食。

translations.literal: Provisions were exhausted; he gathered wild kudzu for food.
translations.idiomatic: When provisions were exhausted, he gathered wild kudzu for food.

sentences.zh: 妻李，遼東巡撫植女，知書明大義，在浙右時，屢脫簪珥佐軍興；

translations.literal: His wife Li, daughter of Grand Coordinator Zhi of Liaodong, was literate and understood great principle; while in western Zhe she repeatedly removed hairpins and earrings to aid military causes;
translations.idiomatic: His wife Li, daughter of Grand Coordinator Zhi of Liaodong, was literate and understood great principle. While in western Zhe she repeatedly removed hairpins and earrings to aid the military cause;

sentences.zh: 偕入剡溪，命二子方岐、方嶷拾墮樵，不以窮阨易操。

translations.literal: she entered Shan Creek with him and had their two sons Fang Qi and Fang Yi gather fallen firewood, not changing their conduct because of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: she entered Shan Creek with him and had their two sons Fang Qi and Fang Yi gather fallen firewood, not changing their conduct because of hardship.

sentences.zh: 適四明山寨競起義軍，以書致玉藻，玉藻思乘間入舟山，為偵騎所遏，不果往。

translations.literal: Just then loyalist camps in Siming sprang up in competition; they wrote inviting Yuzao. Yuzao planned to slip into Zhoushan but was blocked by scouting cavalry and could not go.
translations.idiomatic: Just then loyalist camps in Siming sprang up in competition and wrote inviting Yuzao. Yuzao planned to slip into Zhoushan but was blocked by scouting cavalry and could not go.

sentences.zh: 每臨流讀所作詩，輒激勵慷慨，仰天起舞，或朝夕悲歌，與門人熊亦方相和答。

translations.literal: Whenever by the stream he read poetry he had written, he would be stirred to ardor and lift his face to heaven in dance, or sing mournfully morning and evening, answering each other with his pupil Xiong Yifang.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever by the stream he read poetry he had written, he would be stirred to ardor and lift his face to heaven in dance, or sing mournfully morning and evening, answering each other with his pupil Xiong Yifang.

sentences.zh: 繼亦方以癲死，玉藻歸隱北湖，誓不易衣去發，作絕詞以逝。

translations.literal: Later Yifang died of madness; Yuzao retired in seclusion at North Lake, swearing not to change clothes or cut hair, and composed a final poem before passing away.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yifang died of madness. Yuzao retired in seclusion at North Lake, swearing not to change clothes or cut his hair, and composed a final poem before passing away.

sentences.zh: 遺命不冠而斂。

translations.literal: He left instructions to be buried without a cap.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions to be buried without a cap.

sentences.zh: 李長祥，字研齋，達州人。

translations.literal: Li Changxiang, courtesy name Yanzhai, was a native of Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changxiang, whose courtesy name was Yanzhai, came from Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎癸未進士。

translations.literal: In the guiwei year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the guiwei year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 初以諸生練鄉勇助城守，後選庶吉士，吏部薦備將帥之選。

translations.literal: At first as a student he trained local militia to aid in city defense; later he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and the Ministry of Personnel recommended him for the roster of generals.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as a student, he trained local militia to aid in the city's defense. Later he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and the Ministry of Personnel recommended him for the roster of generals.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「天子果用公，計安出？

translations.literal: Someone said: "If the Son of Heaven truly employs you, sir, what plan would you propose?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "If the Son of Heaven truly employs you, sir, what plan would you propose?

sentences.zh: 」歎曰：「不見孫白谷往事乎？

translations.literal: " He sighed and said: "Have you not seen what happened to Sun Baigu in the past?
translations.idiomatic: " He sighed and said, "Have you not seen what happened to Sun Baigu in the past?

sentences.zh: 今惟有請便宜行事，雖有金牌，亦不受進止。

translations.literal: Today one can only ask to act at discretion; even with a golden tally, one would not accept orders to advance or halt.
translations.idiomatic: Today one can only ask to act at discretion. Even with a golden tally, one would not accept orders to advance or halt.

sentences.zh: 平賊後，囚首闕下受斧鉞耳！

translations.literal: After pacifying the bandits, one would be bound and beheaded beneath the palace gate!"
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the bandits, one would be bound and beheaded beneath the palace gate!"

sentences.zh: 」聞者咋舌。

translations.literal: Those who heard gasped in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard gasped in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 賊日逼，上疏請急令大臣輔太子出鎮津門，以提調勤王兵。

translations.literal: As the rebels pressed daily closer, he memorialized urgently requesting that high ministers escort the crown prince to garrison Jingmen and coordinate relief armies.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels pressed daily closer, he memorialized urgently requesting that high ministers escort the crown prince to garrison Jingmen and coordinate relief armies.

sentences.zh: 不果行，而京師潰，為賊所掠，乘間南奔。

translations.literal: The plan was not carried out; the capital collapsed; he was seized by rebels and slipped away south at an opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was not carried out. The capital collapsed, he was seized by the rebels, and he slipped away south at an opportunity.

sentences.zh: 福王立，改監察御史，巡浙鹽。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he was transferred to investigating censor and toured Zhejiang salt.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he was transferred to investigating censor and toured Zhejiang salt administration.

sentences.zh: 魯王監國，加右僉都御史，督師西行，而江上師又潰。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu assumed regency, he was advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, supervised the army westward, but the river forces collapsed again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu assumed regency, he was advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and supervised the army westward, but the river forces collapsed again.

sentences.zh: 魯王航海去，長祥以餘眾結寨上虞之東山。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu sailed away; Changxiang gathered the remnant force into a camp at Dongshan in Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu sailed away. Changxiang gathered the remnant force into a camp at Dongshan in Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 時浙江諸寨林立，四出募餉，居民苦之。

translations.literal: At that time camps stood thick across Zhejiang, all sallying forth to levy funds, and residents suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time camps stood thick across Zhejiang, all sallying forth to levy funds, and the residents suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 獨長祥與張煌言、王翊三營，且屯且耕，井邑不擾。

translations.literal: Only the three camps of Changxiang, Zhang Huangyan, and Wang Yi both garrisoned and farmed, not disturbing towns and villages.
translations.idiomatic: Only the three camps of Changxiang, Zhang Huangyan, and Wang Yi both garrisoned and farmed, not disturbing towns and villages.

sentences.zh: 監軍鄞人華夏者，為之聯絡佈置，請引舟山之兵，連大蘭諸寨，以定鄞、慈五縣，因下姚江，會師曹娥，合偁山諸寨以下西陵。

translations.literal: The camp inspector Hua Xia of Yin coordinated and arranged matters for them, requesting to bring Zhoushan troops, link the Dalanshan camps, pacify the five counties of Yin and Ci, then descend the Yaojiang, rally at Cao'e, and unite the Weishan camps to advance on Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: The camp inspector Hua Xia of Yin coordinated and arranged matters for them, requesting to bring Zhoushan troops, link the Dalanshan camps, pacify the five counties of Yin and Ci, then descend the Yaojiang, rally at Cao'e, and unite the Weishan camps to advance on Xiling.

sentences.zh: 僉議奉長祥為盟主，刻期將集，而為降紳謝三賓所發，引兵來攻。

translations.literal: All agreed to make Changxiang alliance leader and set a date to assemble, but Xie Sanbin the surrendered gentry betrayed them and led troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed to make Changxiang alliance leader and set a date to assemble, but Xie Sanbin the surrendered gentry betrayed them and led troops to attack.

sentences.zh: 前軍張有功被執，死。

translations.literal: The vanguard commander Zhang Yougong was captured and died.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard commander Zhang Yougong was captured and killed.

sentences.zh: 中軍與百夫長十二人，期以次日縛長祥為獻。

translations.literal: The middle army and twelve centurions agreed to bind Changxiang the next day as their offering.
translations.idiomatic: The middle army and twelve centurions agreed to bind Changxiang the next day and present him as their offering.

sentences.zh: 晨起，十二人忽自相語：「奈何殺忠臣？

translations.literal: At dawn the twelve suddenly said to one another: "How can we kill a loyal minister?
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the twelve suddenly said to one another, "How can we kill a loyal minister?

sentences.zh: 」折矢扣刃，偕誓而遯。

translations.literal: " They broke arrows and notched blades, swore together, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " They broke arrows and notched blades, swore together, and fled.

sentences.zh: 長祥匿丐人舟中，入紹興城。

translations.literal: Changxiang hid in a beggar's boat and entered Shaoxing city.
translations.idiomatic: Changxiang hid in a beggar's boat and entered Shaoxing city.

sentences.zh: 居數日，事益急，复遯至奉化，依平西伯朝先。

translations.literal: After several days' stay, affairs grew still more urgent; he fled again to Fenghua and relied on the Pacifier of the West Chao Xian.
translations.idiomatic: After several days' stay, affairs grew still more urgent. He fled again to Fenghua and relied on the Pacifier of the West Chao Xian.

sentences.zh: 朝先亦蜀人，得其助，復合眾於夏蓋山，晉兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Chao Xian was also a man of Shu; with his help Changxiang regathered forces at Xiagaishan and was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Xian was also a man of Shu. With his help Changxiang regathered forces at Xiagaishan and was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 請合朝先之眾，聯絡沿海，以為舟山衛。

translations.literal: He requested to unite Chao Xian's forces, link the coast, and make Zhoushan a bastion.
translations.idiomatic: He requested to unite Chao Xian's forces, link the coast, and make Zhoushan a bastion.

sentences.zh: 張名振忌之，襲殺朝先，長祥僅免。

translations.literal: Zhang Mingzhen envied him, launched a surprise attack and killed Chao Xian; Changxiang barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mingzhen envied him, launched a surprise attack and killed Chao Xian, and Changxiang barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 舟山破，亡命江、淮間，總督陳錦捕得之，安置江寧。

translations.literal: When Zhoushan fell he fled between the Jiang and Huai; Governor Chen Jin captured him and settled him in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhoushan fell he fled between the Jiang and Huai. Governor Chen Jin captured him and settled him in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乘守者之怠，逸去。

translations.literal: Before long, taking advantage of his guards' negligence, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, taking advantage of his guards' negligence, he escaped.

sentences.zh: 由吳門渡秦郵，奔河北，遍歷宣府、大同，复南下百粵。

translations.literal: From Wumen he crossed to Qinyou, fled to Hebei, traveled through Xuanfu and Datong, then went south again to the hundred Yue.
translations.idiomatic: From Wumen he crossed to Qinyou, fled to Hebei, traveled through Xuanfu and Datong, then went south again to the hundred Yue.

sentences.zh: 晚歲，始還居毗陵，築讀易堂以老。

translations.literal: In his later years he at last returned to live at Piling, built the Hall for Reading the Changes, and grew old there.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he at last returned to live at Piling, built the Hall for Reading the Changes, and grew old there.

sentences.zh: 王正中，字仲扌為，保定人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhengzhong, courtesy name Zhongchi, was a native of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengzhong, whose courtesy name was Zhongchi, came from Baoding.

sentences.zh: 崇禎丁丑進士。

translations.literal: In the dingchou year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the dingchou year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 魯王監國，以兵部職方司主事攝餘姚縣事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu assumed regency, as a principal secretary in the Bureau of Military Appointments of the Ministry of War he acted as magistrate of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu assumed regency, as a principal secretary in the Bureau of Military Appointments of the Ministry of War he served as acting magistrate of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 時義軍猝起，市魁、裡正得一劄付，輒入民舍括金帛，郡縣不敢誰何。

translations.literal: At that time the volunteer armies rose suddenly; ward chiefs and neighborhood wardens, upon receiving a written order, would enter private homes to seize gold and silk, and the prefectures and counties dared not challenge them.
translations.idiomatic: The volunteer armies had sprung up overnight; ward chiefs and neighborhood wardens needed only a written slip to raid private homes for gold and silk, and no prefecture or county dared stand in their way.

sentences.zh: 正中既視事，令各營取餉必經縣，否則以盜論。

translations.literal: Once Zhengzhong had taken office, he ordered that every camp seeking rations must go through the county; otherwise it would be treated as robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhengzhong assumed his post, he decreed that every camp drawing supplies must do so through the county office—or be prosecuted as thieves.

sentences.zh: 總兵陳梧渡海掠餘姚，正中遣民兵擊殺之，諸營大譁，責正中擅殺大將。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief Chen Wu crossed the sea to plunder Yuyao; Zhengzhong sent militia who killed him; the camps clamored loudly, accusing Zhengzhong of killing a general without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: When the commander Chen Wu crossed the sea to loot Yuyao, Zhengzhong dispatched militia who killed him. The camps erupted in uproar, denouncing Zhengzhong for executing a senior general on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 黃宗羲言於監國曰：「梧借喪亂以濟其私，致犯眾怒，是賊也。

translations.literal: Huang Zongxi said to the regent: "Wu used the turmoil of war to serve his private ends, provoking the wrath of the people—he was a bandit."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongxi told the regent, "Wu exploited the chaos of war for private gain and brought the people's wrath upon himself. He was a bandit."

sentences.zh: 正中守土，當為國保民，何罪之有？

translations.literal: Zhengzhong guarded his territory and was duty-bound to protect the people for the state—what crime had he committed?
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhong held his post and was bound to defend the people for the realm—what crime had he committed?

sentences.zh: 」議乃息。

translations.literal: " The dispute then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: " With that, the uproar died down.

sentences.zh: 張國柱、田仰、荊本徹各率所部過姚江，舳艫蔽空而下，以正中嚴備，不敢犯，皆帖帖趣行。

translations.literal: Zhang Guozhu, Tian Yang, and Jing Benche each led their forces past the Yao River; boats and ships filled the sky as they descended; seeing Zhengzhong's strict preparations, they dared not offend and all proceeded submissively on their way.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guozhu, Tian Yang, and Jing Benche each led their troops down the Yao River, their vessels blotting out the sky. Finding Zhengzhong's defenses impenetrable, they dared not provoke him and passed on in docile haste.

sentences.zh: 國柱後從定海入，縱兵焚掠，正中單騎入其軍，呵止之，國柱迄不得逞。

translations.literal: Guozhu later entered from Dinghai and let his troops burn and plunder; Zhengzhong rode alone into his army and shouted them to a halt; Guozhu never got his way.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu later entered through Dinghai and let his men burn and loot at will. Zhengzhong rode alone into the camp and shouted them down. Guozhu never got what he wanted.

sentences.zh: 尋擢監察御史，諸軍從浙西來會，一聽約束，眾倚之若嚴城焉。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to censor; armies coming from western Zhejiang to rendezvous all submitted to his discipline, and the masses relied on him as upon a fortified city.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to censor. Armies arriving from western Zhejiang to muster all submitted to his authority, and the people leaned on him as on a walled fortress.

sentences.zh: 尋以株連繫獄，論死。

translations.literal: Soon he was implicated by association and imprisoned, sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was implicated by association, thrown into prison, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 獄中有閩人柯仲蜅者，精星象，正中欲從受業，援黃霸從夏侯勝授經事為說，數年講習不怠，洞悉天官、律呂、度數諸書，復從黃宗羲學壬遁、孤虛之術。

translations.literal: In prison there was a Fujian man named Ke Zhongbi, skilled in astrology; Zhengzhong wished to study under him, citing the precedent of Huang Ba studying the classics from Xiahou Sheng while in prison; for years they lectured and practiced without slackening; he mastered thoroughly the books on celestial officials, pitch pipes, and measures, and again studied from Huang Zongxi the arts of ren dun and gu xu.
translations.idiomatic: In prison there was a Fujianese named Ke Zhongbi, expert in the stars. Zhengzhong wished to become his pupil and cited the precedent of Huang Ba, who learned the classics from Xiahou Sheng behind bars. For years they lectured without slackening until he had mastered the treatises on celestial offices, pitch pipes, and measures, and then studied under Huang Zongxi the arts of ren dun and gu xu.

sentences.zh: 宗羲歎曰：「傳吾絕學者，仲扌為一人耳！

translations.literal: Zongxi sighed and said: "The one who will transmit my lost learning is Zhongchi alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Zongxi sighed and said, "Of all who might carry on my lost learning, Zhongchi alone will do it!"

sentences.zh: 」遂造監國魯元年丙戌大統歷以進。

translations.literal: " He then compiled the great calendar for the first year of the Prince of Lu's regency, bingxu, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: " He then compiled the great calendar for the bingxu year, the first year of the Prince of Lu's regency, and presented it to the court.

sentences.zh: 浙東亡，避竄山中，貧不能自存，傍鑑湖佃田五畝，佐以醫卜自給。

translations.literal: When eastern Zhejiang fell, he fled into the mountains; too poor to support himself, he rented five mu of land beside Mirror Lake and supplemented his livelihood with medicine and divination.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern Zhejiang fell, he hid in the mountains. Too poor to live, he rented five mu beside Mirror Lake and scraped by with medicine and divination.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Kangxi reign he died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 著有周易註、律書詳註。

translations.literal: He authored Commentaries on the Book of Changes and Detailed Notes on the Pitch-Pipe Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Commentaries on the Book of Changes and Detailed Notes on the Pitch-Pipe Treatise.

sentences.zh: 董守諭，字次公，鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Dong Shouyu, courtesy name Cigong, was a native of Yin County.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shouyu, whose courtesy name was Cigong, came from Yin County.

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He held the provincial graduate degree.

sentences.zh: 魯王監國，召為戶部貴州司主事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu assumed regency, he was summoned as principal secretary in the Guizhou Bureau of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu assumed regency, he was summoned to serve as principal secretary in the Guizhou Bureau of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時熊汝霖、孫嘉績首事起兵，然皆書生，不知調度。

translations.literal: At the time Xiong Rulin and Sun Jiaji first raised troops, but both were literati and knew nothing of military logistics.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiong Rulin and Sun Jiaji had been first to raise arms, but both were scholars who knew nothing of military supply and deployment.

sentences.zh: 乃迎方國安、王之仁，授之軍政，凡原設營兵、衛軍俱隸之。

translations.literal: They therefore welcomed Fang Guo'an and Wang Zhiren and entrusted them with military affairs; all the original camp troops and garrison soldiers were placed under their command.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore brought in Fang Guo'an and Wang Zhiren and handed them military authority; all the original camp troops and garrison soldiers were placed under their command.

sentences.zh: 孫、熊所統，惟召募數百人。

translations.literal: Sun and Xiong commanded only a few hundred recruited men.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and Xiong themselves commanded only a few hundred recruited men.

sentences.zh: 方、王兵既盛，反惡當國者有所參決，因而分餉分地之議起。

translations.literal: Once Fang's and Wang's armies had grown strong, they resented that those governing the state had a say in decisions, and thus arose the debates over dividing rations and dividing territory.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fang's and Wang's forces had grown powerful, they resented the governing ministers' say in affairs, and debate erupted over dividing rations and dividing territory.

sentences.zh: 分餉者，正兵食正餉，田賊之出也，方、王主之；

translations.literal: Dividing rations meant regular troops ate regular rations drawn from land tax and levies, administered by Fang and Wang;
translations.idiomatic: Dividing rations meant regular troops drew regular rations from land tax and levies, under Fang and Wang's control;

sentences.zh: 義兵食義餉，勸捐無名之徵也，熊、孫諸軍主之。

translations.literal: volunteer troops ate volunteer rations from voluntary contributions and unnamed levies, administered by Xiong, Sun, and their armies.
translations.idiomatic: volunteer troops drew volunteer rations from voluntary donations and unscheduled levies, under the control of Xiong, Sun, and their forces.

sentences.zh: 分地者，某正兵，支某邑正餉；

translations.literal: Dividing territory meant a given regular army would draw regular rations from a given district;
translations.idiomatic: Dividing territory meant one regular army would be paid regular rations from one district;

sentences.zh: 某義兵，支某邑義餉也。

translations.literal: a given volunteer army would draw volunteer rations from a given district.
translations.idiomatic: one volunteer army would be paid volunteer rations from one district.

sentences.zh: 魯王令廷臣集議，方、王司餉者，皆至殿陛譁爭，守諭曰：「諸君起義旅，咫尺天威，不守朝廷法乎？

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu ordered court officials to gather for deliberation; Fang's and Wang's supply officers all came to the palace steps clamoring in dispute; Shouyu said: "You gentlemen raised volunteer armies yet stand within arm's reach of the throne's majesty—will you not observe the laws of the court?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu summoned the court to debate the matter. Fang's and Wang's supply officers all crowded the palace steps shouting. Shouyu said, "You raised armies in the cause of righteousness—yet you stand within reach of the throne. Will you not observe the laws of the court?"

sentences.zh: 」乃稍退。

translations.literal: " They then withdrew somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: " They drew back a little.

sentences.zh: 守諭又進曰：「義餉有名無實，以之饋義兵，必不繼。

translations.literal: Shouyu advanced again and said: "Volunteer rations exist in name but not in substance; using them to feed volunteer troops, supplies will surely not be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyu stepped forward again. "Volunteer rations exist in name only. Feed the volunteer armies with them and the supply will not last.

sentences.zh: 即使能繼，誰為管庫？

translations.literal: Even if they could be sustained, who would manage the stores?
translations.idiomatic: Even if they could be sustained, who would keep the accounts and guard the granaries?

sentences.zh: 今請以一切稅供悉歸戶部，計兵而後授餉，覈地之遠近，酌給之後先，則兵不絀於食，而餉可以時給也。

translations.literal: I now propose that all tax revenues be put entirely under the Ministry of Revenue, that rations be granted after tallying troops, weighing proximity of territory and adjusting priority of payment—then troops will not be short of food and rations can be issued on schedule."
translations.idiomatic: I propose that all tax revenues be centralized in the Ministry of Revenue, that rations be allotted only after troops are counted, and that payment be adjusted for distance and priority. Then the armies will not go hungry and supplies can be issued on time."

sentences.zh: 」方、王雖不從，然所議正，無以難也。

translations.literal: " Fang and Wang did not accept, yet what he proposed was correct and they had no way to refute it.
translations.idiomatic: " Fang and Wang would not agree, but his reasoning was sound and they had no answer to it.

sentences.zh: 之仁請收漁船稅，守諭曰：「今日所恃者人心耳，漁戶巳辦漁丁稅矣，若再苛求，民不堪命，人心一搖，國何以立？

translations.literal: Zhiren requested collection of fishing-boat taxes; Shouyu said: "What we rely on today is the hearts of the people; fishing households have already paid the fishing-crew tax—if we demand more, the people cannot bear it; once hearts waver, how can the state stand?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren asked to levy a tax on fishing boats. Shouyu said, "All we have to rely on now is the people's loyalty. Fishing households have already paid the fishing-crew tax. Press them further and they cannot endure it. Once hearts waver, how can the state endure?"

sentences.zh: 」久之，又請行稅人法，請塞金錢湖為田，官賣大戶祀田贍軍，三疏皆下部議，兵士露刃以待覆，守諭力持不可。

translations.literal: " After some time, he again requested the tax-on-persons method, requested damming Gold and Money Lake to reclaim as fields, and requested selling the ancestral temple lands of great households to provision the army—all three memorials were sent down to the ministry for deliberation; soldiers bared blades awaiting the reply; Shouyu firmly insisted they could not be approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he proposed a head tax, damming Mirror Lake to reclaim farmland, and selling the ancestral temple lands of great households to feed the army. All three memorials went to the ministry for review. Soldiers bared their blades awaiting the answer. Shouyu held firm that none of it could be approved.

sentences.zh: 之仁大怒，謂：「行朝大臣不敢裁量幕府，戶曹小臣敢爾阻大事邪？

translations.literal: Zhiren flew into a rage, saying: "Ministers of the mobile court dare not restrain the military headquarters—a petty clerk of the revenue bureau dares thus to obstruct great affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren flew into a rage. "The ministers of the mobile court dare not check the military headquarters—and a petty revenue clerk dares block great affairs like this?"

sentences.zh: 」檄召守諭，將殺之，魯王不能禁，令且避。

translations.literal: " He issued summons for Shouyu intending to kill him; the Prince of Lu could not restrain him and ordered Shouyu to withdraw for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned Shouyu by edict intending to kill him. The Prince of Lu could not stop him and told Shouyu to withdraw for the moment.

sentences.zh: 守諭慷慨對曰：「司餉守正，臣分也。

translations.literal: Shouyu responded boldly: "Managing rations with integrity is my duty as a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyu answered boldly, "To manage rations with integrity is my duty as a minister.

sentences.zh: 生殺出主上，武寧雖悍將，何為者？

translations.literal: Life and death belong to the sovereign; though Wuning is a fierce general, what is he about?
translations.idiomatic: Life and death belong to the sovereign. Wuning may be a fierce general—but what business is it of his?

sentences.zh: 臣任死王前，聽武寧以臣血濺丹墀可耳！

translations.literal: I am willing to die before the king—let Wuning splash my blood upon the crimson steps if he will!"
translations.idiomatic: I am willing to die before the throne. Let Wuning splash my blood on the crimson steps if he will!"

sentences.zh: 」於是舉朝忿怒，曰：「之仁反邪，何敢無王命而害餉臣！

translations.literal: " Then the whole court flared with anger, saying: "Has Zhiren turned rebel? How dare he harm a rations minister without the king's command!"
translations.idiomatic: " The whole court erupted in fury. "Has Zhiren turned traitor? How dare he kill a rations minister without the king's command!"

sentences.zh: 」之仁乃止。

translations.literal: " Zhiren then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhiren then desisted.

sentences.zh: 明年，莊烈帝大祥，守諭請謁朝堂哭，三軍縞素一日，遷經筵日講官，兼理餉事。

translations.literal: The next year, at the great mourning for the Chongzhen Emperor, Shouyu requested an audience to weep in the hall; the three armies wore white mourning for a day; he was promoted to daily lecturer at the Classics Colloquium and concurrently managed rations.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, at the great mourning for the Chongzhen Emperor, Shouyu petitioned to enter the hall and weep. The three armies wore white mourning for a day. He was promoted to daily lecturer at the Classics Colloquium and continued to manage rations.

sentences.zh: 魯王航海，守諭不及從，遂遯跡荒郊，旋卒。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu took to the sea, Shouyu could not follow; he then hid in the wilderness and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu put to sea, Shouyu could not follow. He vanished into the wilds and soon died.

sentences.zh: 著有攬蘭集。

translations.literal: He authored the Collected Writings from Gathering Orchids.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Collected Writings from Gathering Orchids.

sentences.zh: 陸宇，字周明，鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Lu Yu, courtesy name Zhouming, was a native of Yin County.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu, whose courtesy name was Zhouming, came from Yin County.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 慷慨尚氣節。

translations.literal: He was generous and honored integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed and devoted to honor.

sentences.zh: 時有弟子訟其師，師不得直。

translations.literal: At the time a disciple sued his teacher, and the teacher could not obtain justice.
translations.idiomatic: Once a disciple brought suit against his teacher, and the teacher could not obtain justice.

sentences.zh: 宇詣文廟，慟哭伐鼓，卒直其師而後止。

translations.literal: Yu went to the Confucian temple, wept bitterly and beat the drum, and only stopped once his teacher had been vindicated.
translations.idiomatic: Yu went to the Confucian temple, wept and beat the mourning drum, and did not stop until his teacher was vindicated.

sentences.zh: 明亡，嘗與黃宗羲謀舉事，其所與計畫者，皆四方知名士。

translations.literal: After the Ming fell, he once plotted raising an uprising with Huang Zongxi; those with whom he schemed were all renowned men from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Ming, he once plotted an uprising with Huang Zongxi. Those who joined the planning were celebrated men from every quarter of the realm.

sentences.zh: 其城西田舍，複壁柳車，雜賓死友。

translations.literal: At his farmhouse west of the city, with hidden chambers and willow hearses, he concealed fugitives and the friends of the dead.
translations.idiomatic: At his farmhouse west of the city he built hidden chambers and kept willow hearses, sheltering fugitives and the friends of the dead among his guests.

sentences.zh: 計敗，喜事乃益甚。

translations.literal: The plot failed, yet his zealous devotion grew all the stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The plot failed, yet his zeal for the cause only grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 江湖間多傳其姓名，以為異人。

translations.literal: Throughout the rivers and lakes his name circulated widely, and people regarded him as an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: His name traveled through the world of rivers and lakes, and people spoke of him as a man apart.

sentences.zh: 南都破，甬東師起，宇毀家紓餉。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital fell and eastern Ningbo armies rose, Yu ruined his family to relieve the army's rations.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell and armies rose in eastern Ningbo, Yu ruined his family to supply the troops.

sentences.zh: 翁洲又破，宇捐金與諜者，令訪死事消息。

translations.literal: When Weng Isle fell as well, Yu gave gold to spies and had them inquire after news of those who had died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: When Weng Isle fell in turn, Yu gave gold to spies and sent them to learn what had become of those who had died for the cause.

sentences.zh: 張肯堂之孫以俘至，亟治橐饘入獄視之，語其弟宇巇使為脫系。

translations.literal: When the grandson of Zhang Kentang arrived as a captive, he hurriedly prepared food in a bag and entered the prison to visit him, telling his younger brother Lu Xi to arrange his release from custody.
translations.idiomatic: When the grandson of Zhang Kentang was brought in as a prisoner, Yu quickly prepared food in a bag, entered the jail to see him, and told his younger brother Lu Xi to arrange his release.

sentences.zh: 董志寧之喪在海上，宇致而葬之。

translations.literal: Dong Zhining's coffin was at sea; Yu brought it ashore and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhining's body lay at sea; Yu brought it ashore and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 旋為降卒所誣，捕入省獄，獄具，宇無所詿誤，脫械出門，未至館而卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was slandered by surrendered soldiers, arrested and thrown into the provincial prison; when the case was closed Yu had committed no offense and was released from shackles; he died before reaching his lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Soon surrendered soldiers slandered him and he was thrown into the provincial prison. When the case closed he was found guilty of nothing and released from his shackles—but died before he reached his lodging.

sentences.zh: 宇以好事盡其家產，室中所有，惟草薦敗絮及故書數百卷。

translations.literal: Yu had exhausted his family fortune through his passionate devotion to the cause; all that remained in his rooms were straw mats, tattered wadding, and several hundred volumes of old books.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had spent his family's entire fortune in his zeal for the cause. All that remained in his rooms were straw mats, tattered bedding, and a few hundred volumes of old books.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，家人整理其室，得布囊於亂書之下，發而視之，則赫然人頭也。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, his family tidied his room and found a cloth sack beneath disordered books; they opened it and looked—and there plainly was a human head.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his death came, his family tidied his room and found a cloth sack beneath a pile of books. They opened it—and there, plain to see, was a human head.

sentences.zh: 宇巇識其面目，捧之而泣曰：「此故少司馬篤庵王公頭也！

translations.literal: Lu Xi recognized the face, cradled it and wept, saying: "This is the head of the former Vice Minister of War, Lord Wang of Du'an!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xi recognized the face, lifted it in his arms, and wept. "This is the head of the former Vice Minister of War, Lord Wang Du'an!"

sentences.zh: 」初，司馬兵敗，梟城闕，宇思收葬之，每徘徊其下。

translations.literal: " Earlier, when the Vice Minister's army was defeated, his head was displayed at the city gate; Yu had wished to recover and bury it, and often lingered beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, when the Vice Minister's army was defeated, his head was displayed at the city gate. Yu had long wished to recover and bury it, and often lingered beneath the display.

sentences.zh: 一日，見暗中有叩首而去者，蹟之，走入破室。

translations.literal: One day he saw someone in the shadows kowtow and depart; he tracked the man, who fled into a ruined room.
translations.idiomatic: One day he saw someone kowtow in the shadows and slip away. He followed the trail into a ruined room.

sentences.zh: 宇曰：「子何人？

translations.literal: Yu said: "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 」其人曰：「餘毛明山，曾以卒伍事司馬，今不勝故主之感耳！

translations.literal: " The man said: "I am Yu Maomingshan; I once served the Vice Minister as a common soldier; I cannot bear my grief for my old master!"
translations.idiomatic: " The man said, "I am Yu Maomingshan. I once served the Vice Minister as a common soldier. I cannot bear my grief for my old master!"

sentences.zh: 」宇相與流涕，而詣江子云計所以收其頭者。

translations.literal: " Yu wept together with him, then went to Jiang Ziyun to devise how to recover the head.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu wept with him, then went to Jiang Ziyun to plan how to recover the head.

sentences.zh: 子云名漢，錢肅樂部將也。

translations.literal: Ziyun's given name was Han; he had been a subordinate general under Qian Xile.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun's given name was Han. He had been a subordinate general under Qian Xile.

sentences.zh: 失勢家居，會端陽競渡，遊人雜沓，子云紅笠握刀，從十餘人登城遨戲。

translations.literal: Out of power and living at home, on the Dragon Boat Festival when crowds of revelers thronged the streets, Ziyun wore a red hat and gripped a knife, followed by a dozen men onto the city wall in idle sport.
translations.idiomatic: Out of power and living at home, he took advantage of the Dragon Boat Festival, when revelers packed the streets. Ziyun put on a red hat, gripped a knife, and with a dozen followers climbed the city wall in feigned sport.

sentences.zh: 至梟頭所，問守卒曰：「孰戴此頭也者？

translations.literal: Reaching the place where the head was displayed, he asked the guarding soldier: "Whose head is this wearing?"
translations.idiomatic: At the place where the head was displayed, he asked the guard, "Whose head is this?"

sentences.zh: 」卒以司馬對。

translations.literal: " The soldier answered that it was the Vice Minister's.
translations.idiomatic: " The guard answered that it was the Vice Minister's.

sentences.zh: 子云佯怒曰：「嘻！

translations.literal: Ziyun feigned anger and said: "Ha!"
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun feigned rage. "Ha!"

sentences.zh: 吾怨家也，亦有是日乎？

translations.literal: My sworn enemy—and he has this day too?
translations.idiomatic: My sworn enemy—and he has come to this day?

sentences.zh: 」拔刀擊之，繩斷墮地，宇、明山已豫立城下。

translations.literal: " He drew his knife and struck; the rope broke and the head fell to the ground; Yu and Mingshan had already been waiting below the wall.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his knife and struck. The rope snapped and the head fell. Yu and Mingshan were already waiting below the wall.

sentences.zh: 方是時，龍舟噪甚，人無回面易視者，宇以身蔽，明山拾頭雜儔人而去。

translations.literal: Just then the dragon boats made such a clamor that no one turned or glanced aside easily; Yu shielded with his body while Mingshan picked up the head and mingled with the crowd to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the dragon boats raised such a clamor that no one turned to look. Yu shielded the scene with his body while Mingshan picked up the head and slipped away among the crowd.

sentences.zh: 宇祀之書室，蓋十二年矣，而家人無知者。

translations.literal: Yu had enshrined it in his study for some twelve years, yet his family knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had kept it enshrined in his study for some twelve years, and his family knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 至是宇巇始瘞之。

translations.literal: Only now did Lu Xi at last bury it properly.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Lu Xi at last give it proper burial.

sentences.zh: 宇巇，宇第五弟，字春明。

translations.literal: Lu Xi was Yu's fifth younger brother, courtesy name Chunming.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xi was Yu's fifth younger brother; his courtesy name was Chunming.

sentences.zh: 負才自喜，俯視一切。

translations.literal: Talented and self-satisfied, he looked down on everything.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his talent, he looked down on everything around him.

sentences.zh: 宇風格棱棱不可犯，而宇巇稍濟之以和，故世人親之如夏日冬日之分。

translations.literal: Yu's bearing was sharp and forbidding; Lu Xi tempered it somewhat with warmth, so people felt close to them as to summer sun and winter sun respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's manner was austere and forbidding; Lu Xi softened it with warmth. People drew close to them as they do to summer sun and winter sun.

sentences.zh: 然其刻意勵行，雖嚬笑皆歸名節，則一也。

translations.literal: Yet in their deliberate cultivation of conduct, even in frown or smile all returned to integrity—they were one in this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in their deliberate cultivation of virtue, even in a frown or a smile all returned to honor—they were one in that.

sentences.zh: 丙戌後，棄諸生與諸遺民遊，荒亭木末，時聞野哭。

translations.literal: After bingxu he abandoned his licentiate status and wandered with other remnant subjects; in desolate pavilions at the treetops, wild weeping was sometimes heard.
translations.idiomatic: After the bingxu year he gave up his licentiate status and wandered with other loyalist survivors. In ruined pavilions among the treetops, wild weeping could sometimes be heard.

sentences.zh: 同里秀才杜懋俊，仗義死難，藏其遺孤。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman, licentiate Du Maojun, died in righteous martyrdom; he sheltered Du's orphaned child.
translations.idiomatic: Du Maojun, a licentiate from the same town, had died in righteous martyrdom; Lu Xi sheltered his orphaned child.

sentences.zh: 桐城方授，避地來鄞，宇巇館之湖樓中。

translations.literal: Fang Shou of Tongcheng, fleeing the turmoil, came to Yin; Lu Xi lodged him in a lakeside pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shou of Tongcheng, fleeing the chaos, came to Yin. Lu Xi lodged him in a lakeside pavilion.

sentences.zh: 授卒，宇巇經紀其喪，收拾遺文以致其家。

translations.literal: When Shou died, Lu Xi managed his funeral, gathered his surviving writings and sent them to his family.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou died, Lu Xi arranged his funeral, gathered his surviving writings, and sent them to his family.

sentences.zh: 性嗜異書，晚年，家既貧，不能具寫官，乃手鈔之，瀕病不倦。

translations.literal: By nature he loved rare books; in his later years, though his family was poor and could not afford copyists, he copied them by hand, untiring even on the brink of illness.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved rare books. In his later years, when his family was too poor to hire copyists, he copied them by hand himself, tireless even on the edge of death.

sentences.zh: 從子官山左，令其訪東萊趙士喆遺書，垂歿，尚以其書未至為恨。

translations.literal: His nephew served as an official in Shandong; he had him seek out the surviving books of Zhao Shizhe of Donglai; as death approached, he still regretted that those books had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew served as an official in Shandong, and Lu Xi had him seek out the surviving books of Zhao Shizhe of Donglai. As death approached, he still grieved that those books had not arrived.

sentences.zh: 自棄諸生，即練衣蔬食，叢林以為佞佛，爭勸之披緇，宇巇笑不答。

translations.literal: From the time he abandoned his licentiate status he wore plain hemp and ate vegetables; the Buddhist clergy thought him overly devout and all urged him to take the tonsure; Lu Xi smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he gave up his licentiate status he wore plain hemp and ate vegetables. The Buddhist clergy thought him overly pious and urged him to take the tonsure. Lu Xi smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 及遺命不作佛事，眾始瞿然。

translations.literal: When his final instructions forbade Buddhist rites, everyone was startled into realization.
translations.idiomatic: When his final instructions forbade Buddhist rites, everyone was startled into understanding.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 著觀日堂集八卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Collected Writings from the Hall for Observing the Sun, in eight juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Collected Writings from the Hall for Observing the Sun, in eight juan.

sentences.zh: 漢，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Han was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Han came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 為肅樂所倚恃，授以都督僉事總兵官。

translations.literal: Qian Xile relied on him and appointed him regional commander and vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xile relied on him and appointed him regional commander with the rank of vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 師至閩，幾下福州，漢功為多。

translations.literal: When the army reached Fujian and nearly took Fuzhou, Han's achievements were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Fujian and nearly captured Fuzhou, Han's achievements were greatest.

sentences.zh: 侍郎馮景第之乞師日本也，請與偕行。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister Feng Jingdi went to beg troops from Japan, Han requested to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister Feng Jingdi went to Japan to beg for troops, Han asked to go with him.

sentences.zh: 及歸，漢曰：「東師必不出也！

translations.literal: Upon their return, Han said: "The eastern troops will surely not come out!"
translations.idiomatic: On their return, Han said, "The eastern troops will never come out!"

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: " And so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: " And so it proved.

sentences.zh: 肅樂既卒，漢侍母居鄞，種蔬自給，四壁無長物，惟餘肅樂所贈寶刀一而已。

translations.literal: After Xile died, Han attended his mother and lived in Yin, growing vegetables to support himself; his four bare walls held nothing of worth save the precious sword Xile had given him.
translations.idiomatic: After Xile died, Han cared for his mother and lived in Yin, growing vegetables to support himself. His bare rooms held nothing of value save the precious sword Xile had given him.

sentences.zh: 每語及肅樂，則淚淋淋下，抑鬱終。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of Xile, tears streamed down; he ended his days in melancholy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of Xile, tears streamed down his face. He ended his days in grief.

sentences.zh: 方以智，字密之，桐城人。

translations.literal: Fang Yizhi, courtesy name Mizhi, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yizhi, whose courtesy name was Mizhi, came from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 父孔炤，明湖廣巡撫，為楊嗣昌劾下獄，以智懷血疏訟冤，得釋，事具明史。

translations.literal: His father Kong Zhao, Ming Governor-General of Huguang, was impeached by Yang Sichang and imprisoned; Yizhi submitted a blood-stained memorial pleading innocence, obtained release—the matter is fully recorded in the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kong Zhao, the Ming Governor-General of Huguang, was impeached by Yang Sichang and thrown into prison. Yizhi submitted a blood-stained memorial to plead his innocence, and Kong was released—the full account is in the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 以智，崇禎庚辰進士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Yizhi, a jinshi of the gengchen year of Chongzhen, was appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi passed the jinshi examination in the gengchen year of the Chongzhen reign and was appointed a Reviser at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 會李自成破潼關，範景文疏薦以智，召對德政殿，語中機要，上撫幾稱善。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng broke through Tong Pass, Fan Jingwen memorialized recommending Yizhi; summoned for audience at Dezheng Hall, his words hit on essential secrets of state, and the emperor patted the armrest and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng broke through Tong Pass, Fan Jingwen memorialized recommending Yizhi. Summoned for audience at Dezheng Hall, his words struck at the heart of state affairs, and the emperor patted the armrest and praised him.

sentences.zh: 以忤執政意，不果用。

translations.literal: Because he offended the chief ministers' intent, he was not in the end employed.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had offended those in power, he was never actually appointed.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，以智哭臨殯宮，至東華門，被執，加刑毒，兩髁骨見，不屈。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Yizhi wept at the mourning hall; reaching the East Flowery Gate he was seized, subjected to cruel torture until both kneecaps showed bone, yet did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Yizhi went to weep at the mourning hall. At the East Flowery Gate he was seized and tortured until both kneecaps showed bone, yet he would not submit.

sentences.zh: 賊敗，南奔，值馬、阮亂政，修怨欲殺之，遂流離嶺表。

translations.literal: When the rebels were defeated he fled south; encountering the misrule of Ma and Ruan, who nursed old grudges and sought to kill him, he wandered destitute beyond the Lingnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated he fled south. Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng were then misruling the realm, nursing old grudges and seeking his life, and he wandered in exile across the Lingnan frontier.

sentences.zh: 自作序篇，上述祖德，下表隱志。

translations.literal: He wrote a preface himself, above recounting ancestral virtue, below declaring his hidden resolve.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a preface of his own, recounting his family's virtue above and declaring his resolve to live in seclusion below.

sentences.zh: 變姓名，賣藥市中。

translations.literal: He changed his name and sold medicine in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name and sold medicine in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 桂王稱號肇慶，以與推戴功，擢右中允。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Gui assumed title at Zhaoqing, for his merit in supporting the enthronement he was promoted to Right Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Gui assumed the imperial title at Zhaoqing, Yizhi was promoted to Right Supervising Secretary for his role in establishing the regime.

sentences.zh: 扈王幸梧州，擢侍講學士，拜禮部侍郎、東閣大學士，旋罷相。

translations.literal: Escorting the prince to Wuzhou, he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting, appointed Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, then soon removed as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the prince to Wuzhou, he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting, appointed Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, and was soon dismissed from the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 固稱疾，屢詔不起。

translations.literal: He firmly pleaded illness and repeatedly ignored imperial summons.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly pleaded illness and repeatedly refused imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾歸則負君，出則負親，吾其緇乎？

translations.literal: Once he said: "If I return I fail my sovereign; if I go out I fail my parents—shall I take the black robes?
translations.idiomatic: Once he said, "If I return to court I betray my sovereign; if I leave I betray my parents—shall I take the tonsure?

sentences.zh: 行至平樂，被縶。

translations.literal: Traveling to Pingle, he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: On the road to Pingle he was seized.

sentences.zh: 其帥欲降之，左置官服，右白刃，惟所擇，以智趨右，帥更加禮敬，始聽為僧。

translations.literal: The commander wished to win him over: official robes on the left, naked blades on the right—choose as you will. Yizhi moved toward the right; the commander showed him even greater respect and only then allowed him to become a monk.
translations.idiomatic: The commander wished to win him over. Official robes were placed on the left, naked blades on the right—he was free to choose. Yizhi moved toward the blades. The commander treated him with even greater respect and only then allowed him to take the tonsure.

sentences.zh: 更名弘智，字無可，別號藥地。

translations.literal: He changed his name to Hongzhi, courtesy name Wuke, style name Yaodi.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name to Hongzhi, took the courtesy name Wuke, and used the style Yaodi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，赴吉安，拜文信國墓，道卒，其閉關高座時也。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi he went to Ji'an to pay respects at the tomb of Duke Wen of Xin and died on the road—this was during his seclusion at Gaozuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kangxi he set out for Ji'an to pay respects at the tomb of Duke Wen of Xin and died on the road, while still in seclusion at Gaozuo.

sentences.zh: 友人錢澄之，亦客金陵，遇故中官為僧者，問以智，澄之曰：「君豈曾識耶？

translations.literal: His friend Qian Chengshi, also sojourning in Jinling, met a former palace eunuch who had become a monk; asked about Yizhi, Chengshi said: "Did you ever know him?
translations.idiomatic: His friend Qian Chengshi was also staying in Jinling when he met a former palace eunuch who had become a monk. Asked about Yizhi, Chengshi said, "Did you ever know him?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「非也。

translations.literal: " He said: "No.
translations.idiomatic: " The monk said, "No.

sentences.zh: 昔侍先皇，一日朝罷，上忽歎曰：'求忠臣必於孝子！

translations.literal: Formerly I served the late emperor. One day after court was dismissed, the emperor suddenly sighed and said: 'To seek loyal ministers one must look among filial sons!
translations.idiomatic: I once served the late emperor. One day after court was dismissed, the emperor suddenly sighed and said, 'To find loyal ministers one must look among filial sons!

sentences.zh: '如是者再。

translations.literal: ' Thus twice.
translations.idiomatic: ' He said this twice.

sentences.zh: 某跪請故，上曰：'早禦經筵，有講官父巡撫河南，坐失機問大辟，某薰衣，飾容止如常時。

translations.literal: I knelt and asked the reason. The emperor said: 'Early at the Classics Lecture, there was a lecturer whose father was Governor of Henan; for a failure in timing he faced capital punishment. He perfumed his robes and composed his bearing as at ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: I knelt and asked why. The emperor said, 'Early at the Classics Lecture there was a lecturer whose father was Governor of Henan and faced execution for a military failure. He perfumed his robes and carried himself as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 不孝若此，能為忠乎？

translations.literal: So unfilial as this—can he be loyal?
translations.idiomatic: So unfilial as this—how could he be loyal?

sentences.zh: 聞新進士方以智，父亦繫獄，日號泣，持疏求救，此亦人子也。

translations.literal: I hear the newly passed jinshi Fang Yizhi—his father too is imprisoned; day after day he wails and weeps, holding a memorial begging rescue. This too is a human son.'
translations.idiomatic: I hear the newly passed jinshi Fang Yizhi—his father is also in prison. Day after day he weeps and submits memorials begging for rescue. This too is a human son.'

sentences.zh: '言訖复嘆，俄釋孔炤，而辟河南巡撫，外廷亦知其故乎？

translations.literal: Having finished speaking he sighed again; soon Kong Zhao was released and appointed Governor of Henan. Does the outer court also know the reason?
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished he sighed again. Soon Kong Zhao was released and appointed Governor of Henan. Does the outer court know why?

sentences.zh: 」澄之述其語告以智，以智伏地哭失聲。

translations.literal: " Chengshi recounted these words and told Yizhi; Yizhi fell prostrate and wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengshi repeated these words to Yizhi, and Yizhi fell to the ground and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 以智生有異禀，年十五，群經、子、史，略能背誦。

translations.literal: Yizhi was born with unusual endowment; at fifteen he could largely recite from memory the Classics, Masters, and Histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was born with unusual gifts. At fifteen he could largely recite the Classics, Masters, and Histories from memory.

sentences.zh: 博涉多通，自天文、輿地、禮樂、律數、聲音、文字、書畫、醫藥、技勇之屬，皆能考其源流，析其旨趣。

translations.literal: Broadly versed and master of much, from astronomy, geography, rites and music, pitch and number, sound and writing, calligraphy and painting, medicine, and martial skill—he could trace the sources of all and analyze their essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was broad and his mastery deep. From astronomy, geography, rites and music, pitch and number, sound and writing, calligraphy and painting, medicine, and martial skill, he could trace every subject to its sources and analyze its essential meaning.

sentences.zh: 著書數十萬言，惟通雅、物理小識二書盛行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote several hundred thousand characters; only Tongya and Wuli Xiaoshi circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote several hundred thousand characters, but only Tongya and Wuli Xiaoshi circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子中德，字田伯，著古事比。

translations.literal: His son Zhongde, courtesy name Tianbo, authored Gushi Bi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongde, whose courtesy name was Tianbo, wrote Gushi Bi.

sentences.zh: 以智構馬、阮之難，中德年十三，撾登聞鼓，訟父冤。

translations.literal: When Yizhi fell into trouble with Ma and Ruan, Zhongde at thirteen beat the Drum of Heaven's Gate and pleaded his father's injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi fell afoul of Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng, Zhongde at thirteen beat the Drum of Heaven's Gate to plead his father's injustice.

sentences.zh: 父出亡，偕諸弟徒步追從。

translations.literal: When his father fled, he and his brothers followed on foot.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fled into exile, he and his brothers followed on foot.

sentences.zh: 中通，字位伯，精算術，著數度衍，見疇人傳。

translations.literal: Zhongtong, courtesy name Weibo, excelled in mathematics, authored Shudu Yan, and is recorded in the Biographies of Calendar Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongtong, whose courtesy name was Weibo, excelled in mathematics, wrote Shudu Yan, and is recorded in the Biographies of Calendar Masters.

sentences.zh: 中屨，字素伯，幼隨父於方外，備嘗險阻，著古今釋疑。

translations.literal: Zhonglü, courtesy name Subo, from youth followed his father in the world beyond the robe, tasted every hardship, and authored Gujin Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglü, whose courtesy name was Subo, followed his father into monastic life from childhood, endured every hardship, and wrote Gujin Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 錢澄之，字飲光，原名秉鐙，桐城人。

translations.literal: Qian Chengshi, courtesy name Yinguang, original name Bingdeng, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chengshi, whose courtesy name was Yinguang and original name was Bingdeng, came from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 少以名節自勵。

translations.literal: From youth he took integrity as his discipline.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he held himself to the standard of honor.

sentences.zh: 有御史巡按至皖，盛儀從，謁孔子廟，諸生迎迓門外。

translations.literal: When a censor on provincial inspection tour reached Anhui with grand retinue and visited the Confucian temple, the students welcomed him outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When a censor on provincial inspection reached Anhui with a grand retinue and visited the Confucian temple, the students went out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 澄之忽前扳車，御史大駭，止車，因抗聲數其穢行。

translations.literal: Chengshi suddenly stepped forward and seized the carriage; the censor was greatly alarmed and stopped the carriage, whereupon Chengshi raised his voice and denounced his foul conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi suddenly stepped forward and seized the carriage. The censor was alarmed and ordered the carriage stopped, whereupon Chengshi raised his voice and denounced his foul conduct.

sentences.zh: 御史故閹黨，方自幸脫「逆案」，內懼不敢究其事。

translations.literal: The censor was formerly of the eunuch faction and had just congratulated himself on escaping the "treason case"; inwardly afraid, he did not dare pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The censor was a former member of the eunuch faction and had only just congratulated himself on escaping the "treason case." Inwardly afraid, he did not dare pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 澄之以此名聞。

translations.literal: Chengshi became famous for this.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi won fame for this.

sentences.zh: 是時復社、幾社始興，比郡中主壇坫者，宣城沈壽民，池陽吳應箕，桐城則澄之及方以智，而澄之又與陳子龍、夏允彝輩聯雲龍社，以接武東林。

translations.literal: At that time the Fushe and Jishe societies were just rising; in neighboring prefectures those who presided over the literary altars were Shen Shoumin of Xuancheng and Wu Yingji of Chiyang; in Tongcheng, Chengshi and Fang Yizhi; and Chengshi also joined Chen Zilong, Xia Yunyi, and others in the Yunlong Society to carry on the work of the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Fushe and Jishe societies were just rising. In neighboring prefectures Shen Shoumin of Xuancheng and Wu Yingji of Chiyang presided over the literary altars; in Tongcheng it was Chengshi and Fang Yizhi. Chengshi also joined Chen Zilong, Xia Yunyi, and others in the Yunlong Society to carry on the work of the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 澄之體貌偉然，好飲酒，縱談經世之略。

translations.literal: Chengshi was tall and imposing in bearing, loved wine, and discoursed freely on strategies for ordering the age.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi was tall and imposing, loved wine, and spoke freely about strategies for ordering the realm.

sentences.zh: 嘗思冒危難，立功名。

translations.literal: He once thought to brave danger and hardship and establish merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed of braving danger to win merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 阮大鋮既柄用，刊章捕治黨人，澄之先避吳中，妻方赴水死，事具明史。

translations.literal: When Ruan Dacheng came to power, he published edicts to arrest and punish faction members; Chengshi fled first to Wu, and his wife Fang drowned herself—the matter is recorded in the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruan Dacheng came to power and published edicts to arrest faction members, Chengshi fled first to Wu. His wife Fang drowned herself—the full account is in the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 於是亡命走浙、閩，入粵，崎嶇險絕，猶數從鋒鏑間支持名義不少屈。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fled for his life through Zhe and Min into Yue; over rugged and perilous paths he still repeatedly upheld righteous principle amid spear and blade without much yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he fled through Zhejiang and Fujian into Guangdong. Over rugged and perilous paths he still repeatedly upheld righteous principle amid spear and blade, yielding little.

sentences.zh: 黃道周薦諸唐王，授吉安府推官，改延平府。

translations.literal: Huang Daozhou recommended him to the Tang Prince, who appointed him Magistrate of Ji'an Prefecture, then transferred him to Yanping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou recommended him to the Tang Prince, who appointed him Magistrate of Ji'an Prefecture and later transferred him to Yanping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 桂王時，擢禮部主事，特試，授翰林院庶吉士，兼誥敕撰文。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Gui he was promoted to Principal in the Ministry of Rites, passed a special examination, appointed Bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and concurrently drafted edicts and commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Gui he was promoted to Principal in the Ministry of Rites, passed a special examination, appointed a Hanlin Bachelor, and concurrently drafted edicts and commissions.

sentences.zh: 指陳皆切時弊，忌者眾，乃乞假，間道歸里。

translations.literal: His memorials all cut to the evils of the age; those who resented him were many, so he begged leave and returned home by hidden paths.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials all cut to the evils of the age. Resentment against him was widespread, so he begged leave and returned home by hidden paths.

sentences.zh: 結廬先人墓旁，環廬皆田也，自號曰田間，著田間詩學、易學。

translations.literal: He built a hut beside his forebears' tomb; fields surrounded the dwelling on all sides, so he styled himself Tianjian and authored Tianjian Shixue and Yixue.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut beside his forebears' tomb. Fields surrounded the dwelling on all sides, so he styled himself Tianjian and wrote Tianjian Shixue and Yixue.

sentences.zh: 澄之嘗問易道周，依京房、邵雍說，究極數學，後乃兼求義理。

translations.literal: Chengshi once studied the Changes with Daozhou, following the teachings of Jing Fang and Shao Yong to pursue mathematics to its limits, and afterward also sought moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi once studied the Changes with Huang Daozhou, following Jing Fang and Shao Yong to pursue mathematics to its limits, and afterward also sought moral principle.

sentences.zh: 其治詩，遵用小序首句，於名物、訓詁、山川、地理尤詳。

translations.literal: In his study of the Odes he followed the opening lines of the Prefaces and was especially detailed on names and things, glosses, mountains and rivers, and geography.
translations.idiomatic: In his study of the Odes he followed the opening lines of the Prefaces and was especially thorough on names and things, glosses, mountains and rivers, and geography.

sentences.zh: 自謂著易、詩成，思所以翊二經者，而得莊周、屈原，乃復著莊屈合詁。

translations.literal: He said that once his works on the Changes and the Odes were complete, he sought what might support the two Classics and found Zhuang Zhou and Qu Yuan, whereupon he also authored Zhuang-Qu Heigu.
translations.idiomatic: Once his works on the Changes and the Odes were complete, he sought what might support the two Classics and found Zhuang Zhou and Qu Yuan, whereupon he also wrote Zhuang-Qu Heigu.

sentences.zh: 蓋澄之生值末季，離憂抑鬱無所洩，一寓之於言，故以莊繼易，以屈繼詩也。

translations.literal: For Chengshi was born at the dynasty's end; parting and grief, depression with no outlet—all were lodged in words, hence Zhuang followed the Changes and Qu followed the Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi was born at the dynasty's end. Parting, grief, and depression with no outlet he poured into words—hence Zhuang followed the Changes and Qu followed the Odes.

sentences.zh: 又有藏山閣詩文集。

translations.literal: He also had the Cangshange Collected Poetry and Prose.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Cangshange Collected Poetry and Prose.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 惲日初，字仲升，號遜菴，武進人。

translations.literal: Yun Richu, courtesy name Zhongsheng, style Xunan, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Richu, whose courtesy name was Zhongsheng and style was Xunan, came from Wujin.
