sentences.zh: 崇禎癸酉副榜。

translations.literal: Secondary list in the guiyou year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He placed on the secondary list in the guiyou year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 久留京師，應詔上備邊五策，不報。

translations.literal: Long resident in the capital, in response to an edict he submitted five strategies for frontier defense; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: He long remained in the capital. In response to an edict he submitted five strategies for frontier defense, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 知時事不可為，乃歸隱天台山。

translations.literal: Knowing the times could not be set right, he retired to seclusion on Mount Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the times could not be set right, he retired to seclusion on Mount Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 兩京亡，唐王立福州，魯王亦監國紹興，吏部侍郎姜垓薦日初知兵，魯王遣使聘之，固辭不起。

translations.literal: When both capitals fell, the Tang Prince established rule at Fuzhou and the Lu Prince also governed from Shaoxing; Vice Minister of Personnel Jiang Gai recommended Richu as knowledgeable in military affairs, and the Lu Prince sent envoys to invite him, but he firmly declined and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When both capitals fell, the Tang Prince established rule at Fuzhou and the Lu Prince governed from Shaoxing. Vice Minister of Personnel Jiang Gai recommended Richu as knowledgeable in military affairs, and the Lu Prince sent envoys to invite him, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 大兵下浙，避走福州；

translations.literal: When the great army descended on Zhe, he fled to Fuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing army descended on Zhejiang, he fled to Fuzhou;

sentences.zh: 福州破，走廣州；

translations.literal: when Fuzhou fell, he fled to Guangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: when Fuzhou fell, he fled to Guangzhou;

sentences.zh: 廣州复破，乃祝髮為浮圖，復至建陽。

translations.literal: when Guangzhou also fell, he tonsured his head and became a monk, then returned to Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: when Guangzhou also fell, he tonsured his head and became a monk, then went to Jianyang.

sentences.zh: 是時唐王被執死，魯王亦敗走海外，湖廣何騰蛟、江西楊廷麟等皆前後覆滅，而明遺臣尚擁殘旅，遙奉永曆。

translations.literal: At that time the Tang Prince was captured and died, the Lu Prince also fled defeated overseas, He Tengjiao of Huguang and Yang Tinglin of Jiangxi and others were all successively destroyed, yet Ming remnant ministers still held scattered forces and from afar upheld Yongli.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Tang Prince had been captured and killed, the Lu Prince had fled overseas in defeat, and He Tengjiao of Huguang, Yang Tinglin of Jiangxi, and others had been destroyed one after another. Yet Ming loyalist ministers still held scattered forces and from afar upheld the Yongli regime.

sentences.zh: 金壇人王祈聚眾入建寧，屬縣多響應。

translations.literal: Wang Qi of Jintan gathered a host and entered Jianning; many subordinate counties responded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qi of Jintan gathered troops and entered Jianning, and many neighboring counties rose in response.

sentences.zh: 日初曰：「建寧，入閩門戶，能守，則諸郡安，然不扼仙霞關，建寧終不守也。

translations.literal: Richu said: "Jianning is the gateway into Min; if it can be held, the prefectures will be secure—yet without blocking Xianxia Pass, Jianning in the end cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: Richu said, "Jianning is the gateway into Fujian. Hold it and the prefectures will be secure—but without blocking Xianxia Pass, Jianning cannot be held in the end.

sentences.zh: 欲取仙霞，宜先取蒲城。

translations.literal: To take Xianxia, one should first take Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: To take Xianxia, one must first take Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣長子楨隨副將謝南雲先趨蒲城，失利，皆死。

translations.literal: " He then sent his eldest son Zhen with Vice General Xie Nanyun to hurry first to Pucheng; they were defeated and all died.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent his eldest son Zhen with Vice General Xie Nanyun to hurry ahead to Pucheng. They were defeated and all were killed.

sentences.zh: 而御史徐云兵連入數州縣，銳甚，日初說令夜入蒲城，自督兵繼進。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Censor Xu Yun's troops linked victories across several prefectures and counties and were very sharp; Richu persuaded the commander to enter Pucheng by night while he himself led troops in follow-up.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Censor Xu Yun's troops won victory after victory across several prefectures and counties and were very sharp. Richu persuaded the commander to enter Pucheng by night while he himself led troops in support.

sentences.zh: 會大雷雨，人馬衝泥淖，行不能速，軍遂潰。

translations.literal: A great thunderstorm came; men and horses plunged through mud and could not advance quickly, and the army broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A great thunderstorm struck. Men and horses bogged down in mud and could not advance quickly, and the army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 建寧被圍，王使兵部尚書揭重熙赴援。

translations.literal: Jianning was besieged; the prince sent Minister of War Jie Chongxi to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianning was besieged, the prince sent Minister of War Jie Chongxi to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 日初上書，請迳取蒲城，斷仙霞嶺餉道，徐與圍中諸將夾擊之。

translations.literal: Richu submitted a memorial asking to strike directly at Pucheng, cut the supply route over Xianxia Ridge, and then join the besieged generals in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: Richu submitted a memorial asking to strike directly at Pucheng, cut the supply route over Xianxia Ridge, and then join the besieged generals in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 重熙巡至邵武，不能進，建寧遂破，王祈力戰死。

translations.literal: Chongxi patrolled as far as Shaowu but could not advance; Jianning then fell and Wang Qi fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxi reached Shaowu but could advance no farther. Jianning then fell, and Wang Qi fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 日初收殘卒走廣信，尋入封禁山中，數日糧盡，喟然曰：「天下事壞散已數十年，不可救正。

translations.literal: Richu gathered the remnant troops and fled to Guangxin, then entered the Fengjin Mountains; after several days provisions were exhausted, and he sighed and said: "The affairs of the realm have been ruined and scattered for decades—they cannot be set right.
translations.idiomatic: Richu gathered the remnant troops and fled to Guangxin, then entered the Fengjin Mountains. After several days provisions ran out, and he sighed and said, "The affairs of the realm have been ruined and scattered for decades—they cannot be set right.

sentences.zh: 然莊烈帝殉社稷，薄海茹痛，小臣愚妄，謂即此可延天命。

translations.literal: Yet when Emperor Zhuanglie died for the altars of soil and grain, all within the seas tasted grief; this petty subject in foolish presumption thought that by this alone Heaven's mandate might be prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Emperor Zhuanglie died for the realm, grief ran across the land. In my foolish presumption I thought that by this alone Heaven's mandate might still be prolonged.

sentences.zh: 今乃至此，徒毒百姓，何益？

translations.literal: Now it has come to this—only harming the common people. What good is there?
translations.idiomatic: Now it has come to this, harming only the common people. What good does it do?

sentences.zh: 」遂散眾，獨行歸常州。

translations.literal: " He then dismissed the host and returned alone to Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He then dismissed his troops and returned alone to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，張煌言與鄭成功軍薄江寧，敗走。

translations.literal: After a long while, the armies of Zhang Huangyan and Zheng Chenggong approached Jiangning and were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, the armies of Zhang Huangyan and Zheng Chenggong approached Nanjing and were defeated and driven off.

sentences.zh: 訛傳張弟鳳翼乃日初門人，從師匿，縣官將收捕，日初色如常，曰：「吾當死久矣。

translations.literal: A false report spread that Zhang's younger brother Fengyi was Richu's disciple and was hiding with his teacher; the county magistrate was about to arrest him. Richu's countenance was as usual, and he said: "I ought to have died long ago.
translations.idiomatic: A false report spread that Zhang's younger brother Fengyi was Richu's disciple and was hiding with his teacher. The county magistrate was about to arrest him. Richu's face was unchanged, and he said, "I ought to have died long ago.

sentences.zh: 」既而事解。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward the matter was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward the matter was resolved.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十有八。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 少與楊廷樞等交，於百氏無所不窺，尤喜宋儒書。

translations.literal: From youth he associated with Yang Tingji and others, peered into the hundred schools without exception, and especially loved the books of Song Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he associated with Yang Tingji and others, explored the hundred schools without exception, and especially loved the books of Song Confucians.

sentences.zh: 及從劉宗周遊，學益進，嘗上書申

translations.literal: When he followed Liu Zongzhou in study his learning advanced further; once he submitted a memorial pleading for
translations.idiomatic: When he studied under Liu Zongzhou his learning advanced further. Once he submitted a memorial pleading for

sentences.zh: 救，義聲震天下。

translations.literal: rescue, and his righteous appeal shook the world.
translations.idiomatic: rescue, and his righteous appeal shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 丙戌後，累至山陰哭祭，為之行狀，近十萬言。

translations.literal: After bingxu he repeatedly went to Shanyin to weep and offer sacrifice, and wrote a conduct biography for him of nearly a hundred thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: After the bingxu year he repeatedly went to Shanyin to weep and offer sacrifice, and wrote a conduct biography for Liu of nearly a hundred thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 晚服浮圖服，而言學者多宗之。

translations.literal: In his later years he wore Buddhist robes, yet many who spoke of learning looked to him as master.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he wore Buddhist robes, yet many who spoke of learning looked to him as master.

sentences.zh: 無錫高世泰重葺東林書院，日初與同志習禮其間。

translations.literal: Gao Shitai of Wuxi rebuilt the Donglin Academy; Richu and like-minded companions practiced ritual there.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shitai of Wuxi rebuilt the Donglin Academy, and Richu and like-minded companions practiced ritual there.

sentences.zh: 知常州府駱鍾泰屢求見，不納。

translations.literal: Prefect Luo Zhongtai of Changzhou repeatedly sought audience and was not received.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Luo Zhongtai of Changzhou repeatedly sought audience and was refused.

sentences.zh: 去官後，與一見，言中庸要領，喜而去，曰：「不圖今日得聆大儒緒論也！

translations.literal: After leaving office he granted one meeting; speaking on the essentials of the Doctrine of the Mean, Luo departed pleased and said: "I never thought that today I could hear a great scholar's opening discourse!
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office Richu granted one meeting. Speaking on the essentials of the Doctrine of the Mean, Luo departed pleased and said, "I never thought that today I could hear a great scholar's opening discourse!

sentences.zh: 次子桓，在建寧被掠，不知所終；

translations.literal: His second son Huan was captured at Jianning; his end is unknown;
translations.idiomatic: His second son Huan was captured at Jianning, and his fate is unknown;

sentences.zh: 少子格，字壽平，見藝術傳。

translations.literal: his youngest son Ge, courtesy name Shouping, is recorded in the Treatise on Arts.
translations.idiomatic: his youngest son Ge, whose courtesy name was Shouping, is recorded in the Treatise on Arts.

sentences.zh: 郭金台，字幼隗，湘潭人，本姓陳氏，名湜。

translations.literal: Guo Jintai, courtesy name Youwei, was a native of Xiangtan; his original surname was Chen and his name Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jintai, whose courtesy name was Youwei, came from Xiangtan. His original surname was Chen and his given name was Shi.

sentences.zh: 年十五，遭家難，賴中表郭氏卵翼得脫，遂為繼。

translations.literal: At fifteen he suffered a family calamity; relying on his maternal cousin the Guo family to shelter him under wing he escaped, and was thereafter adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he suffered a family calamity. Sheltered by his maternal cousins the Guo family, he escaped and was thereafter adopted into that clan.

sentences.zh: 弱冠有聲黌序間，萬曆間，兩中副車。

translations.literal: In his early manhood he had fame among the schools; in the Wanli reign he twice placed on the secondary list.
translations.idiomatic: In his early manhood he won fame among the schools. During the Wanli reign he twice placed on the secondary list.

sentences.zh: 崇禎朝，屢以名薦，不起；

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he was repeatedly recommended by reputation but would not rise;
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he was repeatedly recommended by reputation but would not accept office;

sentences.zh: 例授官，亦不拜。

translations.literal: when an office was conferred by precedent, he also did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: when an office was conferred by precedent, he also refused.

sentences.zh: 既南渡，隆武鄉試登賢書，督師何騰蛟論薦，授職方郎中。

translations.literal: After crossing south, in the Longwu provincial examination he passed and entered the roster of the worthy; Grand Coordinator He Tengjiao recommended him by memorial and he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing south he passed the Longwu provincial examination. Grand Coordinator He Tengjiao recommended him by memorial, and he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 再起監軍僉事，有司敦迫，皆以母老病辭不就。

translations.literal: When again promoted to Military Supervisor and Vice Commissioner, the local officials pressed him urgently, but each time he declined on the grounds of his mother's age and illness and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When again promoted to Military Supervisor and Vice Commissioner, the local officials pressed him urgently, but each time he declined on the grounds of his mother's age and illness.

sentences.zh: 避跡山中，然於時事多所論列。

translations.literal: He hid his traces in the mountains, yet on current affairs he often set forth opinions.
translations.idiomatic: He hid himself in the mountains, yet on current affairs he often set forth opinions.

sentences.zh: 一二枕戈泣血之士，崎嶇嶺海，經營措置，不遺餘力。

translations.literal: One or two men who slept with weapons at hand and wept blood, over rugged mountains and seas, in planning and arrangement spared no effort.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were one or two warriors who slept with weapons at hand and wept blood in their grief—men who crossed rugged mountains and seas and, in every plan they laid, spared no effort.

sentences.zh: 當是時，潰卒猖獗，積尸盈野，百里無人煙。

translations.literal: At that time routed soldiers ran wild; corpses piled the fields, and for a hundred li there was no sign of human habitation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time routed soldiers ran wild. Corpses piled the fields, and for a hundred li there was no sign of human life.

sentences.zh: 金台請於督師，命偏裨主團練，力率鄉勇，鍛矛戟，峙芻糗，鄉人全活者以數万計。

translations.literal: Jintai petitioned the grand coordinator, who ordered subordinate commanders to oversee militia training; he vigorously led village braves, forged spears and halberds, and stockpiled fodder and dry rations, so that country people who were wholly preserved numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jintai petitioned the grand coordinator, who ordered subordinate commanders to oversee militia training. He vigorously led village braves, forged spears and halberds, and stockpiled fodder and dry rations. Country people who survived because of him numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 清初，當局特疏薦於朝，力請得免。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, the authorities specially memorialized recommending him to the court, but he urgently petitioned and was granted exemption.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qing the authorities specially memorialized recommending him to the court, but he urgently petitioned and won exemption from office.

sentences.zh: 晚授徒衡山，深衣幅巾，足不履戶外，絕口不談世事。

translations.literal: In his later years he taught disciples at Hengshan, wearing the deep robe and headcloth; his feet never crossed the threshold, and he never spoke of worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he taught disciples at Hengshan, dressed in the deep robe and headcloth of a scholar. His feet never crossed the threshold, and he never spoke of worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 惟論列當時殉難諸人，輒欷歔流涕。

translations.literal: Only when he set forth those who had died for the cause in that age would he sigh and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he spoke of those who had died for the cause in that age would he sigh and weep.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年，以疾卒於家，年六十有七。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he died of illness at home, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he died of illness at home, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 自題其墓曰「遺民郭某之墓」。

translations.literal: He himself inscribed his tomb: "The tomb of Guo, a leftover subject."
translations.idiomatic: He himself inscribed his tomb: "The tomb of Guo, a leftover subject."

sentences.zh: 著有石村詩文集，五經駢語，博物彙編。

translations.literal: His writings include Shicun Collected Poems and Prose, Parallel Sayings on the Five Classics, and Compendium of Natural History.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Shicun Collected Poems and Prose, Parallel Sayings on the Five Classics, and Compendium of Natural History.

sentences.zh: 硃之瑜，字魯興，號舜水，餘姚人，寄籍松江。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhiyu, courtesy name Luxing, art name Shunshui, was a native of Yuyao with registered residence at Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhiyu, whose courtesy name was Luxing and art name Shunshui, was a native of Yuyao with registered residence at Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 少有志概，九歲喪父，哀毀逾禮。

translations.literal: In youth he had lofty resolve; at nine he lost his father and mourned beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had lofty resolve. At nine he lost his father and mourned beyond what the rites prescribed.

sentences.zh: 及長，精研六經，特通毛詩。

translations.literal: When grown, he deeply studied the Six Classics and was especially versed in the Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he deeply studied the Six Classics and was especially versed in the Mao Odes.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，以諸生兩奉徵闢，不就。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chongzhen reign, as a common scholar he twice received imperial summons but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign, as a common scholar he twice received imperial summons but refused to accept office.

sentences.zh: 福王建號江南，召授江西按察司副使，兼兵部職方司郎中，監方國安軍，之瑜力辭。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu established his reign in Jiangnan, he was summoned and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, concurrently Director in the Bureau of Appointments of the Ministry of War, to supervise the army of Fang Guo'an; Zhiyu forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu established his reign in Jiangnan, Zhiyu was summoned and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, concurrently Director in the Bureau of Appointments of the Ministry of War, to supervise the army of Fang Guo'an. He forcefully declined.

sentences.zh: 台省劾偃蹇不奉詔，將逮捕，乃走避舟山，與經略王翊相締結，密謀恢復。

translations.literal: The censorial offices impeached him for defiance in not obeying the edict and were about to arrest him, so he fled to Zhoushan, formed a bond with Grand Coordinator Wang Yi, and secretly plotted restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial offices impeached him for defiance in not obeying the edict and were about to arrest him. He fled to Zhoushan, formed a bond with Grand Coordinator Wang Yi, and secretly plotted restoration.

sentences.zh: 渡海至日本，思乞師。

translations.literal: He crossed the sea to Japan, intending to beg for military aid.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the sea to Japan, intending to beg for military aid.

sentences.zh: 魯王監國，累徵闢，皆不就。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu served as regent, he was repeatedly summoned but each time refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu served as regent, Zhiyu was repeatedly summoned but each time refused.

sentences.zh: 又赴安南，見國王，強令拜，不為屈，轉敬禮之。

translations.literal: He again went to Annam and saw the king, who forced him to bow; he would not yield, and the king in turn treated him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: He again went to Annam and saw the king, who forced him to bow. He would not yield, and the king in turn treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 復至日本，時舟山既失，之瑜師友擁兵者，如硃永祐、吳鍾巒等皆已死節，乃決蹈海全節之志，遂留寓長崎。

translations.literal: He returned again to Japan; by then Zhoushan had already fallen, and Zhiyu's teachers and friends who held troops, such as Zhu Yongyou and Wu Zhongluan, had all died for the cause, so he resolved on the will to cast himself into the sea and preserve his integrity intact, and thereupon took up residence at Nagasaki.
translations.idiomatic: He returned again to Japan. By then Zhoushan had already fallen, and Zhiyu's teachers and friends who held troops—Zhu Yongyou, Wu Zhongluan, and others—had all died for the cause. He resolved to preserve his integrity even at the cost of casting himself into the sea, and thereupon took up residence at Nagasaki.

sentences.zh: 日人安東守約等師事之，束脩敬養，始終不衰。

translations.literal: Japanese such as Ando Moriyasu took him as master, presenting teacher's gifts and supporting him with respect, which never waned to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese scholars such as Ando Moriyasu took him as master, presenting teacher's gifts and supporting him with respect—a devotion that never waned to the end.

sentences.zh: 日本水戶侯源光國厚禮延聘，待以賓師，之瑜慨然赴焉。

translations.literal: Mito lord Minamoto Mitsukuni of Japan treated him with generous courtesy and extended an invitation, receiving him as guest and teacher; Zhiyu went forth with solemn resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Mito lord Minamoto Mitsukuni of Japan treated him with generous courtesy and extended an invitation, receiving him as guest and teacher. Zhiyu went forth with solemn resolve.

sentences.zh: 每引見談論，依經守義，曲盡忠告善道之意。

translations.literal: Whenever summoned to audience for discussion, he held to the classics and upheld righteousness, fully expounding the intent of loyal counsel and good guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever summoned to audience for discussion, he held to the classics and upheld righteousness, fully expounding loyal counsel and good guidance.

sentences.zh: 教授學者，循循不倦。

translations.literal: In instructing scholars he was methodical and never weary.
translations.idiomatic: In instructing scholars he was methodical and never weary.

sentences.zh: 日人重之瑜，禮養備至，特於壽日設養老之禮，奉几杖以祝。

translations.literal: The Japanese esteemed Zhiyu and treated him with every courtesy in provision and support; on his birthday they specially performed the ceremony for venerating the aged, presenting table and staff in blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese esteemed Zhiyu and treated him with every courtesy in provision and support. On his birthday they specially performed the ceremony for venerating the aged, presenting table and staff in blessing.

sentences.zh: 又為製明室衣冠使服之，並欲為起居第，之瑜再辭曰：「吾藉上公眷顧，孤踪海外，得養志守節，而保明室衣冠，感莫大焉！

translations.literal: They also had Ming court dress made for him to wear, and wished to build him a residence as well; Zhiyu again declined, saying: "Through my lord's gracious care, alone and far overseas, I have been able to nourish my will and keep my integrity, and to preserve Ming court dress—my gratitude is beyond measure!
translations.idiomatic: They also had Ming court dress made for him to wear, and wished to build him a residence as well. Zhiyu again declined, saying: "Through my lord's gracious care, alone and far overseas, I have been able to nourish my will and keep my integrity, and to preserve Ming court dress—my gratitude is beyond measure!

sentences.zh: 吾祖宗墳墓，久為發掘，每念及此，五內慘烈。

translations.literal: The tombs of my ancestors have long been dug up; whenever I think of this, my innermost being is torn with anguish.
translations.idiomatic: The tombs of my ancestors have long been dug up. Whenever I think of this, my innermost being is torn with anguish.

sentences.zh: 若豐屋而安居，豈我志乎？

translations.literal: If I lived in a grand house at ease, would that be my will?
translations.idiomatic: If I lived in a grand house at ease, would that be my will?

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they stopped.

sentences.zh: 之瑜為日人作學宮圖說，商榷古今，剖微索隱，使梓人依其圖而以木模焉，棟樑枅椽，莫不悉備。

translations.literal: Zhiyu wrote an illustrated explanation of the school palace for the Japanese, comparing ancient and modern, probing the subtle and seeking the hidden; he had carpenters follow his drawings and make wooden models, with pillars, beams, bracket-sets, and rafters all fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu wrote an illustrated explanation of the school palace for the Japanese, comparing ancient and modern usage and probing every subtle detail. He had carpenters follow his drawings and make wooden models, with pillars, beams, bracket-sets, and rafters all fully provided.

sentences.zh: 而殿堂結構之法，梓人所不能通曉者，親指授之。

translations.literal: As for methods of hall and shrine construction that the carpenters could not fully understand, he personally instructed them point by point.
translations.idiomatic: As for methods of hall and shrine construction that the carpenters could not fully understand, he personally instructed them point by point.

sentences.zh: 度量分寸，湊離機巧，教喻縝密，經歲而畢。

translations.literal: Measuring inches and fractions, fitting joints with mechanical ingenuity, his teaching was meticulous; a full year passed before it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring inches and fractions and fitting joints with mechanical ingenuity, his teaching was meticulous. A full year passed before the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 文廟、啟聖宮。

translations.literal: The Confucian temple and the Hall of the Sage's Origin.
translations.idiomatic: The Confucian temple and the Hall of the Sage's Origin.

sentences.zh: 明倫堂、尊經閣、學舍、進賢樓，廊廡射圃，門戶牆垣，皆極精巧。

translations.literal: The Hall of Illuminating Human Relations, the Pavilion for Honoring the Classics, student quarters, the Tower for Advancing the Worthy, corridors, the archery ground, gates, and walls—all were exquisitely crafted.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Illuminating Human Relations, the Pavilion for Honoring the Classics, student quarters, the Tower for Advancing the Worthy, corridors, the archery ground, gates, and walls—all were exquisitely crafted.

sentences.zh: 又造古祭器，先作古升、古尺，揣其稱勝，作簠、簋、籩、豆、登、鉶之屬。

translations.literal: He also made ancient sacrificial vessels, first fashioning ancient sheng and ancient chi, gauging their proper proportions, then making fu, gui, bian, dou, deng, xing, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He also made ancient sacrificial vessels, first fashioning ancient sheng and ancient chi and gauging their proper proportions, then making fu, gui, bian, dou, deng, xing, and the like.

sentences.zh: 如周廟欹器，唐、宋以來，圖雖存而製莫傳，乃依圖考古，研覈其法，巧思默契，指畫精到。

translations.literal: Such as the tipping vessel of the Zhou temple: from Tang and Song onward, though illustrations survived, the craft was not transmitted; he therefore followed the illustrations to investigate antiquity, studied and verified the method, matched it with ingenious thought, and directed the work with precise detail.
translations.idiomatic: Such as the tipping vessel of the Zhou temple: from Tang and Song onward, though illustrations survived, the craft was not transmitted. He followed the illustrations to investigate antiquity, studied and verified the method, matched it with ingenious thought, and directed the work with precise detail.

sentences.zh: 授之工師，或未洞達。

translations.literal: When he passed the work to master craftsmen, some still did not fully grasp it.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed the work to master craftsmen, some still did not fully grasp it.

sentences.zh: 復為揣輕重，定尺寸，關機運動，教之經年，不厭煩數，卒成之。

translations.literal: He again gauged weight and balance, fixed dimensions, and adjusted the moving mechanism; he taught them for a full year, never weary of repetition, and at last completed it.
translations.idiomatic: He again gauged weight and balance, fixed dimensions, and adjusted the moving mechanism. He taught them for a full year, never weary of repetition, and at last completed it.

sentences.zh: 於是率儒學生，習釋奠禮，改定儀注，詳明禮節，學者皆通其梗概。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led Confucian students in practicing the sacrificial ceremony, revised the ritual regulations, and explained the rites in detail, so that the scholars all mastered their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he led Confucian students in practicing the sacrificial ceremony, revised the ritual regulations, and explained the rites in detail, so that the scholars all mastered their essentials.

sentences.zh: 日人文教，為之彬彬焉。

translations.literal: Japanese culture and learning thereby became refined and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese culture and learning thereby became refined and flourishing.

sentences.zh: 之瑜居日本二十餘年，年八十三卒，葬於日本長崎瑞龍山麓。

translations.literal: Zhiyu lived in Japan for more than twenty years; he died at eighty-three and was buried at the foot of Ruilong Mountain in Nagasaki, Japan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu lived in Japan for more than twenty years. He died at eighty-three and was buried at the foot of Ruilong Mountain in Nagasaki, Japan.

sentences.zh: 日人諡曰文恭先生，立祠祀之，並護其墓，至今不衰。

translations.literal: The Japanese posthumously titled him Master Wengong, erected a shrine to sacrifice to him, and also guarded his tomb—a devotion that has not waned to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese posthumously titled him Master Wengong, erected a shrine to sacrifice to him, and also guarded his tomb—a devotion that has not waned to this day.

sentences.zh: 之瑜嚴毅剛直，動必以禮。

translations.literal: Zhiyu was stern, resolute, and upright; in every movement he held to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu was stern, resolute, and upright; in every movement he held to ritual.

sentences.zh: 平居不苟言笑，唯言及國難，常切齒流涕。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he was not careless in speech or laughter; only when he spoke of the nation's calamity would he gnash his teeth and weep.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary life he was not careless in speech or laughter. Only when he spoke of the nation's calamity would he gnash his teeth and weep.

sentences.zh: 魯王敕書，奉持隨身，未嘗示人，歿後始出，人皆服其深密謹厚雲。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu's written command he kept on his person and never showed to others; only after his death did it come forth, and all admired his discretion and scrupulous integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu's written command he kept on his person and never showed to others. Only after his death did it come forth, and all admired his discretion and scrupulous integrity.

sentences.zh: 著有文集二十五卷，釋奠儀註一卷，陽九述略一卷，安南供役紀事一卷。

translations.literal: His writings include Collected Works in twenty-five juan, one juan of Ritual Notes on the Sacrificial Ceremony, one juan of Brief Account of Yangjiu, and one juan of Record of Service in Annam.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Collected Works in twenty-five juan, one juan of Ritual Notes on the Sacrificial Ceremony, one juan of Brief Account of Yangjiu, and one juan of Record of Service in Annam.

sentences.zh: 沈光文，字文開，一字斯菴，鄞人。

translations.literal: Shen Guangwen, courtesy name Wenkai, also styled Sian, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Guangwen, whose courtesy name was Wenkai and who also styled himself Sian, was a native of Yin.

sentences.zh: 少以明經貢太學，福王授太常博士，浮海至長垣，晉工部郎。

translations.literal: In youth, through mastery of the classics, he was presented to the Imperial Academy; the Prince of Fu appointed him Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he crossed the sea to Changyuan and was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, through mastery of the classics, he was presented to the Imperial Academy. The Prince of Fu appointed him Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He crossed the sea to Changyuan and was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 閩師潰而北，扈從不及。

translations.literal: When the Fujian army collapsed and fled north, he could not follow in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fujian army collapsed and fled north, he could not follow in attendance.

sentences.zh: 聞粵中建號，乃走肇慶，累遷太僕卿。

translations.literal: Hearing that a reign title had been raised in Guangdong, he hastened to Zhaoqing and was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that a reign title had been raised in Guangdong, he hastened to Zhaoqing and was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 由潮陽航海至金門，閩督李率泰方招徠故國遺臣，密遣使以書幣招之，光文焚書返幣。

translations.literal: From Chaoyang he sailed to Jinmen; Fujian Governor Li Shuaitai was then recruiting leftover subjects of the former dynasty and secretly sent an envoy with letters and gifts to summon him; Guangwen burned the letters and returned the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: From Chaoyang he sailed to Jinmen. Fujian Governor Li Shuaitai was then recruiting leftover subjects of the former dynasty and secretly sent an envoy with letters and gifts to summon him. Guangwen burned the letters and returned the gifts.

sentences.zh: 知粵事不可支，卜居於泉州海口，浮家泛宅。

translations.literal: Knowing that affairs in Guangdong could not be sustained, he chose to dwell at the mouth of Quanzhou harbor, living on boats as his home.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that affairs in Guangdong could not be sustained, he chose to dwell at the mouth of Quanzhou harbor, living on boats as his home.

sentences.zh: 忽颶風大作，舟人失維，飄泊至台灣。

translations.literal: Suddenly a great hurricane arose; the boatmen lost their moorings and were driven to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a great hurricane arose. The boatmen lost their moorings and were driven to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功尚未至，而台灣為荷蘭所據，光文受一廛以居，與中土音耗隔絕。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Chenggong had not yet arrived, and Taiwan was held by the Dutch; Guangwen received one plot of land to dwell on and was cut off from all word from the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng Chenggong had not yet arrived, and Taiwan was held by the Dutch. Guangwen received one plot of land to dwell on and was cut off from all word from the central lands.

sentences.zh: 成功克台灣，知光文在，大喜，以賓禮見。

translations.literal: When Chenggong conquered Taiwan and learned that Guangwen was there, he was greatly pleased and received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenggong conquered Taiwan and learned that Guangwen was there, he was greatly pleased and received him with guest ceremony.

sentences.zh: 時海上諸遺老，多依成功入台，光文與握手相勞苦。

translations.literal: At that time many old loyalists of the coast followed Chenggong to Taiwan; Guangwen clasped hands with them and shared their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many old loyalists of the coast followed Chenggong to Taiwan. Guangwen clasped hands with them and shared their hardships.

sentences.zh: 成功致廩餼，且以田宅贍之。

translations.literal: Chenggong supplied him with grain rations and also provided fields and a residence for his support.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong supplied him with grain rations and also provided fields and a residence for his support.

sentences.zh: 成功卒，子錦嗣，改父之臣與政，軍亦日削。

translations.literal: When Chenggong died, his son Jing succeeded; he changed his father's ministers and policies, and the army also daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenggong died, his son Jing succeeded. Jing changed his father's ministers and policies, and the army also daily declined.

sentences.zh: 光文作賦諷之，幾不測。

translations.literal: Guangwen wrote a rhapsody satirizing him and nearly came to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwen wrote a rhapsody satirizing him and nearly came to disaster.

sentences.zh: 乃變服為浮屠，逃入台北鄙，結茅羅漢門山中以居，山旁有伽溜灣者，番社也。

translations.literal: He then changed his dress and became a Buddhist monk, fled into the remote north of Taipei, and built a thatched hut in the Luohan Gate mountains to dwell; beside the mountain was Jialiu Bay, an aboriginal settlement.
translations.idiomatic: He then changed his dress and became a Buddhist monk, fled into the remote north of Taipei, and built a thatched hut in the Luohan Gate mountains to dwell. Beside the mountain was Jialiu Bay, an aboriginal settlement.

sentences.zh: 光文教授生徒自給，不足，則濟以醫。

translations.literal: Guangwen taught students to support himself; when that was not enough, he supplemented it with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwen taught students to support himself. When that was not enough, he supplemented his income with medicine.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「吾二十載飄零絕島，棄墳墓不顧者，不過欲完發以見先皇帝於地下耳，而卒不克，命也夫！

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "For twenty years I have drifted on a remote island and abandoned my ancestral tombs, wanting nothing but to keep my hair whole and meet the late emperor in the underworld—yet in the end I could not; it is fate!
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said: "For twenty years I have drifted on a remote island and abandoned my ancestral tombs, wanting nothing but to keep my hair whole and meet the late emperor in the underworld—yet in the end I could not. It is fate!

sentences.zh: 」已而錦卒，諸鄭復禮之如故。

translations.literal: " Before long Jing died, and the Zheng clan again treated him with the same courtesy as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Jing died, and the Zheng clan again treated him with the same courtesy as before.

sentences.zh: 康熙癸丑年，王師下台灣，閩督姚啟聖招之，光文辭。

translations.literal: In the guichou year of Kangxi, when the imperial army descended on Taiwan, Fujian Governor Yao Qisheng summoned him, but Guangwen declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year of Kangxi, when the imperial army descended on Taiwan, Fujian Governor Yao Qisheng summoned him, but Guangwen declined.

sentences.zh: 啟聖貽書問訊曰：「管寧無恙？

translations.literal: Qisheng sent a letter of inquiry, saying: "Is Guan Ning well?
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng sent a letter of inquiry, saying: "Is Guan Ning well?

sentences.zh: 」且許遣人送歸鄞，會啟聖卒，不果。

translations.literal: " He also promised to send someone to escort him back to Yin, but Qisheng died before it could be done.
translations.idiomatic: " He also promised to send someone to escort him back to Yin, but Qisheng died before it could be done.

sentences.zh: 而諸羅令李麟光，賢者也，為粟肉之繼，旬日一候門下。

translations.literal: But Magistrate Li Linguang of Zhuluo was a worthy man who supplied grain and meat in succession, calling at his gate every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: But Magistrate Li Linguang of Zhuluo was a worthy man who supplied grain and meat in succession, calling at his gate every ten days.

sentences.zh: 時耆宿已盡，而寓公漸集，乃與宛陵韓文琦，關中趙行可，無錫華袞、鄭廷桂，榕城林奕丹，山陽宗城，螺陽王際慧等結詩社，所稱福台新詠者也。

translations.literal: By then the old worthies were all gone, but exiles from abroad gradually gathered; he then formed a poetry society with Han Wenqi of Wancheng, Zhao Xingke of Guanzhong, Hua Gun and Zheng Tinggui of Wuxi, Lin Yidan of Rongcheng, Zong Cheng of Shanyang, Wang Jihui of Luoyang, and others—the group known as Fudai New Poems.
translations.idiomatic: By then the old worthies were all gone, but exiles from abroad gradually gathered. He then formed a poetry society with Han Wenqi of Wancheng, Zhao Xingke of Guanzhong, Hua Gun and Zheng Tinggui of Wuxi, Lin Yidan of Rongcheng, Zong Cheng of Shanyang, Wang Jihui of Luoyang, and others—the group known as Fudai New Poems.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於諸羅。

translations.literal: Before long he died at Zhuluo.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died at Zhuluo.

sentences.zh: 陳士京，字佛莊，先世本奉化硃氏，遷鄞，改姓陳。

translations.literal: Chen Shijing, courtesy name Fozhuang, was originally of the Zhu clan of Fenghua; his ancestors moved to Yin and changed their surname to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shijing, whose courtesy name was Fozhuang, was originally of the Zhu clan of Fenghua. His ancestors moved to Yin and changed their surname to Chen.

sentences.zh: 熊汝霖薦授職方司郎中，監三衢總兵陳謙軍。

translations.literal: Xiong Rulin recommended him and he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Appointments, to supervise the army of Chen Qian, Regional Commander of Sanqu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Rulin recommended him and he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Appointments, to supervise the army of Chen Qian, Regional Commander of Sanqu.

sentences.zh: 謙使閩，偕行，而唐、魯方爭頒詔事，謙死，遂遯之海上。

translations.literal: When Qian was sent on mission to Fujian, Shijing went with him; but the Tang and Lu courts were then contending over the issuance of edicts, Qian died, and Shijing thereupon fled to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian was sent on mission to Fujian, Shijing went with him. But the Tang and Lu courts were then contending over the issuance of edicts. Qian died, and Shijing thereupon fled to the sea.

sentences.zh: 鄭芝龍聞名，令與其子成功遊，芝龍以閩降，成功不肯從，異軍特起，士京實讚之。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhilong, hearing of his reputation, had him associate with his son Chenggong; when Zhilong surrendered Fujian, Chenggong refused to follow and raised a separate force on his own, which Shijing in fact applauded.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhilong, hearing of his reputation, had him associate with his son Chenggong. When Zhilong surrendered Fujian, Chenggong refused to follow and raised a separate force on his own, which Shijing in fact applauded.

sentences.zh: 已而汝霖奉魯王室，復以公義說成功，始致寓公之敬。

translations.literal: Before long Rulin served the court of the Prince of Lu; Shijing again appealed to Chenggong on grounds of public duty, and only then did Chenggong show him the respect due a guest in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Rulin served the court of the Prince of Lu. Shijing again appealed to Chenggong on grounds of public duty, and only then did Chenggong show him the respect due a guest in exile.

sentences.zh: 會魯王上表粵中，成功亦欲啟事於粵，使士京往，加都御史，歸。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu submitted a memorial in Guangdong, Chenggong also wished to open relations with Guangdong and sent Shijing; he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu submitted a memorial in Guangdong, Chenggong also wished to open relations with Guangdong and sent Shijing. Shijing was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and returned.

sentences.zh: 魯王入浙，特留閩，與成功相結，以為後圖。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu entered Zhejiang, Shijing was specially left in Fujian to form a bond with Chenggong for future plans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu entered Zhejiang, Shijing was specially left in Fujian to form a bond with Chenggong for future plans.

sentences.zh: 成功盛以恢復自任，賓禮遺臣，其最致敬者，尚書盧若騰，侍郎王忠孝，都御史章朝薦，及徐孚遠、沈光文，與士京數人而已。

translations.literal: Chenggong greatly took upon himself the task of restoration and treated leftover subjects with guest ceremony; those to whom he showed the greatest respect were Minister Lu Ruoteng, Vice Minister Wang Zhongxiao, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Chaojian, Xu Fuyuan, Shen Guangwen, and Shijing among a few others.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong greatly took upon himself the task of restoration and treated leftover subjects with guest ceremony. Those to whom he showed the greatest respect were Minister Lu Ruoteng, Vice Minister Wang Zhongxiao, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Chaojian, Xu Fuyuan, Shen Guangwen, and Shijing among a few others.

sentences.zh: 久之，見海師無功，粵事亦日壞，乃築鹿石山房於鼓浪嶼中，感物賦詩以自遣。

translations.literal: After a long while, seeing that the maritime forces achieved nothing and affairs in Guangdong also daily worsened, he built the Lushi Mountain Studio on Gulangyu and, moved by things around him, composed poems to console himself.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, seeing that the maritime forces achieved nothing and affairs in Guangdong also daily worsened, he built the Lushi Mountain Studio on Gulangyu and, moved by things around him, composed poems to console himself.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 吳祖錫，字佩遠，吳江人。

translations.literal: Wu Zuxi, courtesy name Peiyuan, was a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zuxi, whose courtesy name was Peiyuan, was a native of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎壬午副貢。

translations.literal: In the renshen year of Chongzhen he placed on the secondary list.
translations.idiomatic: In the renshen year of Chongzhen he placed on the secondary list.

sentences.zh: 時中原大亂，料京師必危，預謀勤王。

translations.literal: At that time the central plains were in great disorder; he foresaw that the capital would surely be imperiled and planned in advance to rush to the emperor's aid.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the central plains were in great disorder. He foresaw that the capital would surely be imperiled and planned in advance to rush to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 欲身任浙西，以浙東屬之許都，約未定而變作，故鎮臣陳洪範隨王師下江南，與有舊，自言其降出於不得已，而以奇策告祖錫，立出遺產四萬金畀之。

translations.literal: He wished to take western Zhejiang upon himself and assign eastern Zhejiang to Xu Du, but before the agreement was settled the crisis broke out; former garrison commander Chen Hongfan followed the Qing army south into Jiangnan, had old ties with him, said himself that his surrender was from necessity, and told Zuxi a bold stratagem, immediately producing forty thousand taels of gold from his inherited estate and giving it to him.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to take western Zhejiang upon himself and assign eastern Zhejiang to Xu Du, but before the agreement was settled the crisis broke out. Former garrison commander Chen Hongfan followed the Qing army south into Jiangnan. They had old ties, and Hongfan said his surrender had been from necessity. He told Zuxi a bold stratagem and immediately produced forty thousand taels of gold from his inherited estate and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 已而薙發令下，遽委之去，改名鉏，字稽田。

translations.literal: Before long the order to shave the head was issued; he abruptly entrusted the matter to others and left, changing his name to Chu and his courtesy name to Jitian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the order to shave the head was issued. He abruptly entrusted the matter to others and left, changing his name to Chu and his courtesy name to Jitian.

sentences.zh: 從陳子龍、徐孚遠謀恢復。

translations.literal: He followed Chen Zilong and Xu Fuyuan in plotting restoration.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chen Zilong and Xu Fuyuan in plotting restoration.

sentences.zh: 偵事杭州，為仇家縛送江寧，羈繫獄中，复髡而縱之。

translations.literal: While scouting affairs at Hangzhou, he was bound by an enemy family and sent to Jiangning, detained in prison, shaved again, and then released.
translations.idiomatic: While scouting affairs at Hangzhou, he was bound by an enemy family and sent to Jiangning. He was detained in prison, shaved again, and then released.

sentences.zh: 魯王授職方郎中，桂王亦官之如魯，仍往來吳、越間。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu appointed him Director in the Bureau of Appointments; the Prince of Gui also gave him office like that under Lu, and he still traveled back and forth between Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu appointed him Director in the Bureau of Appointments. The Prince of Gui also gave him office like that under Lu, and he still traveled back and forth between Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 副將馮源淮駐軍嘉興，乃與結納，冀有所為。

translations.literal: Vice General Feng Yuanhuai was stationed at Jiaxing, and Zuxi formed a bond with him, hoping to accomplish something.
translations.idiomatic: Vice General Feng Yuanhuai was stationed at Jiaxing, and Zuxi formed a bond with him, hoping to accomplish something.

sentences.zh: 其部屬董某司诇察，馮耳目也，亦故與厚善。

translations.literal: A subordinate of his, one Dong, handled reconnaissance and was Feng's eyes and ears; he was also formerly on close terms with Zuxi.
translations.idiomatic: A subordinate of his, one Dong, handled reconnaissance and was Feng's eyes and ears. He was also formerly on close terms with Zuxi.

sentences.zh: 比孚遠歸自海外，有所謀，密館之。

translations.literal: When Fuyuan returned from overseas with plans afoot, Zuxi secretly lodged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuyuan returned from overseas with plans afoot, Zuxi secretly lodged him.

sentences.zh: 事稍聞於馮，馮遣董詣問，祖錫遽前握其手曰：「徐公在此，若欲見之乎？

translations.literal: The matter was slightly heard by Feng, who sent Dong to inquire; Zuxi at once stepped forward, grasped his hand, and said: "Master Xu is here—do you wish to see him?
translations.idiomatic: The matter was slightly heard by Feng, who sent Dong to inquire. Zuxi at once stepped forward, grasped his hand, and said: "Master Xu is here—do you wish to see him?

sentences.zh: 」董驚曰：「徐公果在此，顧肯令我見耶？

translations.literal: " Dong said in alarm: "If Master Xu is truly here, would he really let me see him?
translations.idiomatic: " Dong said in alarm: "If Master Xu is truly here, would he really let me see him?

sentences.zh: 」即引見，董叩頭泣下，道其鄉慕，矢不相負。

translations.literal: " He was at once led to an audience; Dong kowtowed and wept, spoke of his longing for home, and swore he would not betray them.
translations.idiomatic: " He was at once led to an audience. Dong kowtowed and wept, spoke of his longing for home, and swore he would not betray them.

sentences.zh: 因以譌言報馮，而陰遣弋船衛孚遠浮海去。

translations.literal: He therefore reported false words to Feng, while secretly dispatching archer boats to escort Fuyuan away by sea.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore reported false words to Feng, while secretly dispatching patrol boats to escort Fuyuan away by sea.

sentences.zh: 海師入江，祖錫實導之，且連歲在金陵，隱為之助。

translations.literal: When the maritime forces entered the Yangtze, Zuxi in fact guided them, and for successive years at Jinling he secretly aided them.
translations.idiomatic: When the maritime forces entered the Yangtze, Zuxi in fact guided them. For successive years at Jinling he secretly aided them.

sentences.zh: 乃復遭刊章，事解，志不稍挫。

translations.literal: He then again suffered a published warrant for arrest, but when the matter was resolved his will was not in the least broken.
translations.idiomatic: He then again suffered a published warrant for arrest, but when the matter was resolved his will was not in the least broken.

sentences.zh: 將詣滇南，而先之鄖陽。

translations.literal: He was about to go to southern Yunnan, but first went to Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to go to southern Yunnan, but first went to Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 時鄖陽十三營，尚保殘寨，乃勸出師撓楚以救滇。

translations.literal: At that time the Thirteen Camps at Yunyang still held remnant strongholds, and he urged them to march out and harass Chu to relieve Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Thirteen Camps at Yunyang still held remnant strongholds, and he urged them to march out and harass Chu to relieve Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 顧十三營已疲敝，不能用其策也。

translations.literal: But the Thirteen Camps were already exhausted and worn, and could not employ his plan.
translations.idiomatic: But the Thirteen Camps were already exhausted and worn, and could not employ his plan.

sentences.zh: 桂王既入緬甸，思追從，道阻，不得達。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Gui had entered Burma, Zuxi thought to follow after him, but the road was blocked and he could not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Gui had entered Burma, Zuxi thought to follow after him, but the road was blocked and he could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 復返吳。

translations.literal: He returned again to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He returned again to Wu.

sentences.zh: 遊中州，更由秦入楚，卒無所遇。

translations.literal: He traveled through the central provinces, then from Qin into Chu, and in the end met with nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled through the central provinces, then from Qin into Chu, but in the end found no opportunity.

sentences.zh: 康熙己未，客膠州大竹山，鬱鬱靡所騁​​。

translations.literal: In the jiwei year of Kangxi he lodged as a guest at Dazhushan in Jiaozhou, depressed with nowhere to deploy his talents.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year of Kangxi he lived as a guest at Dazhushan in Jiaozhou, depressed and with no outlet for his abilities.

sentences.zh: 會懷宗忌日，慟哭嘔血死，遺命藁葬山中，年​​六十有二。

translations.literal: It happened to be the memorial day of the Chongzhen Emperor; he wailed until he vomited blood and died, leaving instructions to be buried in a simple grave in the mountains, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: On the memorial day of the Chongzhen Emperor he wailed until he vomited blood and died. He left instructions for a simple burial in the mountains. He was sixty-two years old.

sentences.zh: 距明亡已三十有五年矣。

translations.literal: It was already thirty-five years since the fall of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-five years had passed since the fall of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 凡明末三王遺臣逸士，其初或起義，或言事，各有所謀，其後或蹈海，或居夷，志不少沮，皆先後雲亡。

translations.literal: In general, the surviving ministers and reclusive scholars of the three Ming princes at the end of the dynasty—at first some raised righteous armies, some remonstrated in office, each with his own design; afterward some went to sea, some lived among foreigners, their resolve little diminished, and all passed away one after another like clouds dispersing.
translations.idiomatic: In general, the loyalist officials and reclusive scholars who served the three Ming princes at the dynasty's end first raised armies or remonstrated in office, each pursuing his own design. Later some fled across the sea and some lived abroad, yet their resolve scarcely wavered until, one after another, they passed away like clouds dispersing.

sentences.zh: 及祖錫死，徐枋為之傳曰：「自吳子歿，而天下絕援溺之望。

translations.literal: When Zuxi died, Xu Fang wrote his biography, saying: "Since Master Wu's death, the world's hope of rescuing the drowning has been cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuxi died, Xu Fang wrote his biography, saying, "Since Master Wu's death, the world's hope of rescuing the drowning has been cut off.

sentences.zh: 」亦可悲矣！

translations.literal: " How lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: " How lamentable that is!

sentences.zh: 故以附於明末遺臣之末。

translations.literal: Therefore he is appended at the end of the late-Ming surviving ministers.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason his account is appended among the late-Ming loyalist officials.
